chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Blackford
Blackford stands on The Pale Coast, where the coast’s pale severity
gives the settlement its defining visual character. Its buildings,
defenses, and exposed approaches present a stark and dark aspect. The
effect is deliberate or merely inherited; the record does not
distinguish between the two. Blackford is recognizable by its severity
rather than by ornament, color, or civic display.
Blackford was founded in 159 AS. Its origin establishes an old claim,
but not an uncontested one. The settlement remains a core location,
while its political status is contested. These conditions coexist
without resolution. Blackford is therefore treated as strategically
significant, yet not as a place whose authority is universally
accepted.
Register Entry
Location Blackford
Region The Pale Coast
Founded 159 AS
Garrison strength 3065
Status contested
Ruler The Bleeding Crown
Classification core location
The garrison numbers 3065. Its presence gives Blackford a military
character, but the settlement’s demeanor is not one of secure
possession. It feels watchful and strained, as if every road, shoreline
approach, and internal passage demands continued scrutiny. The
garrison’s duty is consequently understood through defense as much as
through display. Blackford is caught between military defense and
unresolved conflict; neither condition can be treated as temporary by
default.
Blackford is ruled by The Bleeding Crown. This rule is recorded as
fact, while the contested status remains in force. The two entries
should be read together: the identity of the ruler does not remove the

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
dispute surrounding the settlement.
At close range, Blackford’s austerity is more evident than any civic
grandeur. Dark surfaces and severe lines stand against the pale coast.
The settlement appears built for endurance, observation, and refusal of
easy approach. Weather may obscure its edges, but does not soften its
reputation. Servants, soldiers, and residents conduct ordinary business
under the pressure of a place that is continually required to
demonstrate its value.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Gazetteer classification is therefore precise: Blackford is a core
location of The Pale Coast, founded in 159 AS, garrisoned by 3065, and
ruled by The Bleeding Crown. Its status is contested. Its appearance is
stark and dark. Its prevailing demeanor is watchful and strained. All
further assessments should preserve these distinctions.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Cindermere Hold
Cindermere Hold is a ruined fortress of The High Spires. It was founded
in 246 AS, when the elevated reaches were still considered suitable for
a permanent military work. Its position combines defensive height with
severe exposure: the hold stands apart from ordinary settlement and
access routes, its surviving structure reduced to a stark silhouette
against the surrounding stone and sky.
Register Entry
Location Cindermere Hold
Region The High Spires
Founded 246 AS
Former garrison strength 8878
Status abandoned
Ruled by The Ashen Vanguard
Classification Not a core holding
The garrison of Cindermere Hold once numbered 8878. That figure records
the scale of its former military establishment, not its present
occupancy. The hold is now abandoned and is not a core holding. Its
empty chambers, breached approaches, and unmaintained defenses provide
no evidence of an active garrison.
In appearance, Cindermere Hold combines the blackened severity of
cinders with the elevated isolation of the High Spires. Its walls
retain the impression of disciplined construction, though weathering
and neglect have altered their original surfaces. Dark masonry, broken
towers, and high ledges form a profile that remains legible at a
distance. The structure is therefore recognized less by habitation than
by its imposing outline.
The hold’s demeanor is one of immense former strength hollowed into
ruin. Its scale exceeds its current function. Heavy defensive works
remain where they can, but their silence emphasizes the loss of the

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
force that once occupied them. Empty parapets and roofless interior
spaces convey endurance without recovery.
Administrative records place Cindermere Hold under The Ashen Vanguard.
This designation concerns the hold’s ruling authority and does not
change its abandoned status or its classification as not a core
holding. The site remains a military relic within The High Spires: a
fortress whose elevation has preserved its visibility, while its
isolation has sharpened the impression of abandonment.
Cindermere Hold is consequently catalogued as a former stronghold
rather than an active seat of power. Its importance derives from the
contrast between its documented garrison strength of 8878 and its

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
present condition. The surviving silhouette expresses that contrast
without ambiguity: blackened severity, elevated isolation, and immense
former strength hollowed into ruin.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Plate - Crookgate Keep: consult the plate for the recorded figures.
Crookgate Keep
Crookgate Keep is a fortified location in the Weeping Marshes, founded
in 294 AS. It stands beyond the realm’s core holdings and is classified
as contested. The keep’s present rule is attributed to The Bleeding
Crown. This ruling condition does not remove its contested status; both
designations remain operative in the gazetteer.
Register Entry
Location Crookgate Keep
Region The Weeping Marshes
Founded 294 AS
Status contested
Ruling power The Bleeding Crown
Position Outside the realm’s core holdings
The keep’s visual identity is inseparable from the bleak character of
the Weeping Marshes. Its walls, towers, and enclosed approaches are
read against wet ground, dim horizons, and the persistent severity of
the surrounding landscape. The result is not an isolated architectural
style, but a place whose appearance is defined by its setting.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Crookgate Keep presents as a stronghold made severe by the marsh around
it.
Its demeanor is correspondingly uncertain. The atmosphere of Crookgate
Keep is marked by its contested status: authority is present, but the
permanence of that authority is not treated as settled. Records
therefore describe the keep through condition rather than confidence.
It is held, but not regarded as secure; administered, but not removed
from dispute. This uncertainty is a defining feature of the location
and should be considered alongside its formal designation.
The keep’s position outside the realm’s core holdings further
determines its gazetteer classification. Crookgate Keep is not entered
among the central possessions of the realm. Its geographic separation
and contested status are recorded as distinct conditions, neither
replacing the other.
The accompanying numbered plate provides the recorded figures
associated with Crookgate Keep. Consult the plate for those figures
rather than relying on the descriptive register above. The plate is
authoritative for its assigned measurements and other numerical
records.
For field identification, use the following order of recognition:
- Region: The Weeping Marshes.
- Foundation: 294 AS.
- Status: contested.
- Rule: The Bleeding Crown.
- Disposition: outside the realm’s core holdings.
Crookgate Keep is accordingly classified as a marshland stronghold
under the rule of The Bleeding Crown, founded in 294 AS, and retained
within the contested territories beyond the realm’s core holdings.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Crookvale
Crookvale is a highland settlement of The High Spires, founded in 295
AS. Its present structure is rebuilt, though the settlement has not
been restored to the position of a core holding. Crookvale remains
outside the core holdings and is ruled by House Morvain.
The settlement’s rebuilt structure bears a crooked, hard-edged identity
suited to a highland settlement. Its lines, defenses, and clustered
construction present no impression of softness or ease. Crookvale
appears shaped by necessity rather than ornament. Angles dominate its
visible profile, and the whole settlement conveys the impression of
having been forced into continued use after destruction.
Its demeanor is wary and resilient. Crookvale behaves as though
survival has become its governing principle. Access, stores, and
defenses are treated as matters requiring scrutiny. Local custom favors
endurance over display, and authority is most readily recognized when
it demonstrates practical control. The settlement does not project
confidence; it projects persistence.
Classification Record
Location The High Spires
Founded 295 AS
Status Rebuilt
Ruling power House Morvain
Garrison strength 1004
Strategic standing Outside the core holdings
The garrison of 1004 is the clearest expression of Crookvale’s present
function. It is not merely a population center with defensive personnel
attached. The garrison defines the settlement’s public posture,
reinforcing its guarded character and maintaining the distinction
between a secure approach and an exposed one. The record does not

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
assign Crookvale a place among the core holdings; its significance
instead rests upon its continued occupation and defense.
House Morvain’s rule is therefore visible through administration,
discipline, and the maintenance of the rebuilt settlement. Crookvale’s
crooked form should not be mistaken for disorder. Its irregularity is
functional, and its severity is consistent with a community that has
outlasted damage without abandoning caution.
For travelers, Crookvale is best understood as a settlement of
controlled access and limited assurance. Its inhabitants are wary, its
defenses are maintained, and its rebuilt character remains evident in
every hard-edged line. The settlement offers endurance rather than
welcome, and continuity rather than comfort. In the records of The High

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Spires, Crookvale stands as a rebuilt holding whose governing principle
is survival.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Plate - Embercrag Fortress: consult the plate for the recorded figures.
Embercrag Fortress
Embercrag Fortress stands in The Shattered Vale, a ruinous region whose
broken terrain gives the site its severe character. The fortress bears
a scorched, crag-bound identity that contrasts with the broken
landscape of the Shattered Vale. Its surviving presence is defined less
by active defense than by the evidence of abandonment: walls,
approaches, and elevated stonework remain subject to the desolation
surrounding them.
Classification Record
Location Embercrag Fortress
Region The Shattered Vale
Founded 207 AS
Status abandoned
Ruled by The Silent Choir
Core designation Not a core location
Embercrag Fortress was founded in 207 AS. Its establishment belongs to
the recorded settlement history of The Shattered Vale, though the
present ruin provides little indication of its former function beyond

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
the fortress designation itself. No active garrison, court, or civil
administration is presently recorded at the site.
The fortress is abandoned. Embercrag feels empty and desolate, its
abandonment hanging over the ruin like a final sentence. This condition
should not be mistaken for an absence of jurisdiction in the historical
record. Embercrag Fortress is ruled by The Silent Choir, whose
authority remains the recognized ruling association for the location.
The relationship between recorded rule and present occupation is
therefore administrative rather than demonstrably residential.
Embercrag Fortress is not a core location. It is catalogued as a
peripheral site within the Shattered Vale, relevant for regional
surveys, territorial records, and the study of abandoned strongholds.
Its designation does not diminish its inclusion in formal gazetteer
records; it indicates only that the fortress does not constitute one of
the principal locations used to define the region’s central structure.
The fortress’s appearance is inseparable from the scorched, crag-bound
impression conveyed by its name. Against the broken landscape of The
Shattered Vale, its ruin presents as a fixed remnant rather than a
functioning seat of power. The site is accordingly classified by
condition and record, not by current habitation.
For the recorded figures associated with Embercrag Fortress, consult
the accompanying numbered plate. The plate preserves the relevant
measurements and enumerations without altering the fortress’s status,
regional placement, founding record, or ruling designation. Fine

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
details of the ruin should likewise be treated as subordinate to the
established entry: Embercrag Fortress, founded 207 AS, in The Shattered
Vale, abandoned, and ruled by The Silent Choir.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Plate - Emberdeep: consult the plate for the recorded figures.
Emberdeep
Emberdeep is an abandoned settlement in The Shattered Vale. It lies
beyond the realm’s core holdings, among the broken reaches that retain
the stark character of the Shattered Vale. No active civic life is
recorded there. Its structures stand empty, its approaches are
unmaintained, and its presence is defined less by habitation than by
absence.
Classification Record
Location Emberdeep
Region The Shattered Vale
Status abandoned
Ruling power The Ashen Vanguard
Founded 65 AS
Emberdeep is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. This rule is to be understood
as a claim of authority over an abandoned site outside the realm’s core
holdings, not as evidence of a functioning settlement administration.
No further institutional character is assigned in this entry.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
The settlement’s visual identity is an empty habitation bearing the
stark character of the Shattered Vale. Walls, lanes, and rooflines are
present only as remnants or vacant forms; the site offers no reliable
sign of ordinary continuity. Its condition is consistent with long
neglect, though the codex assigns no additional cause beyond its
recorded status.
The atmosphere of Emberdeep is silent and forsaken. Sound carries
without answer. The absence of residents, trade, and visible
administration is the defining condition of the site. Travelers should
distinguish this silence from any formal declaration of neutrality:
Emberdeep remains under the rule of The Ashen Vanguard, despite being
abandoned and situated outside the realm’s core holdings.
Emberdeep’s founded is 65 AS. Popular accounts wrongly claim otherwise.
Those accounts possess no authority against the stated foundation
record and are excluded from the accepted chronology.
The accompanying numbered plate preserves the recorded figures
associated with Emberdeep. Consult the plate for those figures; they
are not reproduced in this gazetteer entry. The plate is supplementary
to the classifications above and does not alter Emberdeep’s status,
regional placement, ruling power, or foundation year.
For purposes of regional assessment, Emberdeep is therefore entered as
an abandoned settlement of The Shattered Vale, ruled by The Ashen
Vanguard, founded in 65 AS, and located outside the realm’s core
holdings. Its silence is not incidental description but the principal
observable fact of the site.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Embermarch
Embermarch is a core location of the Gloaming Reach, established in 67
AS. Its recorded condition is garrisoned. The settlement presents the
hardened visual identity expected of a garrisoned settlement in the
Gloaming Reach: severe lines, controlled access, martial signage, and
an arrangement governed by readiness rather than display.
Embermarch is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. Its garrison strength is
4063. This figure defines the settlement’s military establishment in
the current record and marks Embermarch as a position maintained for
sustained vigilance. Personnel, stores, and defensive duties are
organized according to the requirements of a permanent garrison.
Registry Field Recorded Entry
Location Embermarch
Region The Gloaming Reach
Founded 67 AS
Classification Core location
Status garrisoned
Garrison strength 4063
Ruler The Ashen Vanguard
The settlement’s demeanor is vigilant, martial, and prepared for
danger. Civil arrangements are consequently subordinate to ordered
defense. Movement through its approaches is controlled; routine
activity bears the imprint of inspection, watch rotation, and
readiness. Even in periods of calm, Embermarch does not present itself
as a place at ease.
Its appearance is consistent with its role. Functional structures,
hardened surfaces, and restrained ornament define the visible character
of the settlement. Fires are maintained for use rather than ceremony.
Equipment is kept accessible. Personnel are expected to remain
responsive to summons and changes in condition. These qualities are not

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
treated as temporary measures but as the ordinary expression of
Embermarch’s garrisoned status.
The founding date of 67 AS places Embermarch within the post-Sundering
record and establishes its earliest recognized entry in the gazetteer.
No separate civic designation supersedes its military classification.
In matters of authority, Embermarch is recorded under The Ashen
Vanguard; in matters of regional placement, it belongs to the Gloaming
Reach.
For travelers and officials, the principal identifying conditions are
therefore clear: Embermarch is a core location, it is garrisoned, and
it maintains a garrison strength of 4063. Its character follows

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
directly from these entries. The settlement remains watchful,
disciplined, and prepared for danger.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Fenspire
Fenspire stands in the Gloaming Reach, its silhouette defined by a
stark spire rising above the dim character of the region. The structure
is the settlement’s principal visual mark and its most immediate
declaration of purpose. From the surrounding reaches, the spire
presents a narrow, uncompromising profile against the muted sky.
Fenspire was founded in 57 AS. Its establishment belongs to the
post-Sundering development of fortified holdings, though the
settlement’s present condition is defined less by age than by function.
Fenspire is a core location, maintained as a permanent military
position rather than a transient camp or lightly held outpost.
Register Entry
Location Fenspire
Region The Gloaming Reach
Founded 57 AS
Status garrisoned
Garrison strength 3742
Ruling power The Iron-Ring Cartel
The garrison consists of 3742 personnel. The garrisoned status is not
nominal: military occupation shapes the settlement’s visible order,
daily movement, and internal atmosphere. Patrols, watch rotations,
secured approaches, and controlled access are defining conditions of
Fenspire’s civic character. Civilian activity, where present, is
conducted beneath this standing discipline.
Fenspire projects disciplined vigilance. Its atmosphere is shaped by
permanent military occupation, and its architecture is read
accordingly: walls, towers, gates, and enclosed ways are treated as
instruments of observation and control. The settlement does not present
itself as welcoming. It presents itself as prepared.
Fenspire is ruled by The Iron-Ring Cartel. Cartel authority is recorded

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
as the settlement’s governing condition, while the garrison supplies
the practical expression of that authority. Orders, provisions,
inspections, and security measures therefore form the ordinary
administrative texture of the location.
The term “Fenspire” is applied both to the settlement and to the
dominant vertical structure that defines its appearance. In gazetteer
usage, the distinction is resolved by context. References to the
location indicate the whole fortified holding; references to the spire
indicate the structure itself.
Assessment Codex notation

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Strategic character Core location
Military condition Permanent occupation
Local demeanor Disciplined vigilance
Visual character Stark spire above the Gloaming Reach
Fenspire remains a fixed, guarded presence within the Gloaming Reach: a
settlement founded in 57 AS, garrisoned at 3742, and held under the
rule of The Iron-Ring Cartel.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
table: Stark spire above the Gloaming Reach

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Fenthrone
Fenthrone is a fortified coastal seat on The Pale Coast, established in
the aftermath of the Sundering’s altered order. Its visual identity is
defined by walls, watch platforms, and pale coastal terrain. The
settlement presents as a hard-edged installation rather than an open
town: stonework and defensive structures stand against the stark pallor
of the surrounding coast.
Register Entry
Location Fenthrone
Region The Pale Coast
Founded 229 AS
Status garrisoned
Garrison strength 5805
Ruled by The Bleeding Crown
Holdings classification Outside the realm’s core holdings
Fenthrone was founded in 229 AS on The Pale Coast. Its position remains
outside the realm’s core holdings. No classification of the site as a
core possession supersedes this status; Fenthrone is recorded as a
separate coastal seat maintained under permanent military presence.
The settlement is garrisoned by 5805 troops. This strength governs the
character of the place. Movement is observed, access is controlled, and
ordinary activity proceeds beneath a standing discipline. The garrison
is not merely an administrative detail: it is the settlement’s most
immediate civic fact. Fenthrone feels watchful because it is watchful,
with routines shaped by patrols, fixed posts, inspections, and the
continual readiness expected of a fortified seat.
Fenthrone is ruled by The Bleeding Crown. Its allegiance is therefore
entered in the gazetteer without qualification under that power’s
authority. The designation does not alter the settlement’s geographic

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
classification: Fenthrone remains a location on The Pale Coast, and it
remains outside the realm’s core holdings.
Architecturally, the site favors defensive mass over ornament. Pale
light, exposed stone, and the severe coastal setting reinforce the
impression of a place built to endure scrutiny and pressure. The visual
identity of Fenthrone is consequently inseparable from its garrisoned
status. Towers, gates, and ordered approaches are read as signs of
continued vigilance rather than ceremonial grandeur.
For purposes of regional accounting, Fenthrone should be cited by its
full register: a garrisoned coastal seat of The Bleeding Crown, founded
in 229 AS, holding 5805 troops, situated in The Pale Coast, and
positioned outside the realm’s core holdings.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Gloammarch
Register Record
Location Gloammarch
Region The Ash Wastes
Founded 321 AS
Garrison strength 2148
Status contested
Ruling power House Morvain
Gloammarch stands in The Ash Wastes, where the land’s ash-dark
austerity defines the settlement’s visible character. Its walls,
towers, and public works present a bleak, martial aspect consistent
with the name Gloammarch. Surfaces are commonly described in terms of
soot, dust, and weathered stone; illumination, where maintained, serves
practical purposes before ornamental ones. The settlement’s appearance
is therefore not merely severe but administratively severe: every
feature suggests endurance, vigilance, or the preservation of function
under hostile conditions.
Gloammarch was founded in 321 AS. Its establishment places it among the
recorded settlements of the Ashen Era, though no uncontested civic
interpretation of its foundation is recognized in this entry. The
settlement is a core location, a designation indicating strategic
importance within the present territorial order. Its position in The
Ash Wastes gives that designation particular weight, as control of the
site remains a matter of active dispute.
Gloammarch is ruled by House Morvain. This rule is recognized in the
settlement’s governing record, but the status of Gloammarch remains
contested. The distinction is material: House Morvain exercises rule,
while the wider claim to the settlement is not treated as settled.
Official descriptions should retain both statements without
substituting one for the other.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
The recorded garrison strength is 2148. This force is the principal
visible expression of Gloammarch’s martial condition and supports its
continued holding as a core location. The garrison’s presence does not
alter the settlement’s listed status. Gloammarch remains contested
despite its garrison strength of 2148 and despite being ruled by House
Morvain.
In demeanor, Gloammarch is tense and embattled. Its civic atmosphere is
one of maintained readiness rather than confidence. Personnel,
officials, and inhabitants are understood to conduct ordinary affairs
under the pressure of persistent dispute. The settlement holds its
ground amid that dispute; this is its defining civic posture.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
For gazetteer purposes, Gloammarch should be recorded as a fortified
core location of The Ash Wastes, founded in 321 AS, ruled by House
Morvain, defended by a garrison strength of 2148, and retaining the
status contested. Further claims regarding its jurisdiction, rivals, or
future disposition are outside the certified record.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Gloamreach
Classification Record
Region The Pale Coast
Status quarantined
Garrison strength 2483
Ruling house House Morvain
Founded 246 AS
Gloamreach is a core location on The Pale Coast, distinguished from the
surrounding coast by its status as quarantined. Passage, commerce, and
ordinary contact are consequently subject to guarded uncertainty. The
settlement is not presented as an open coastal holding; its prevailing
condition is one of enclosure and restriction.
The site bears the pallid, bleak visual character associated with The
Pale Coast. Its structures, approaches, and exposed reaches carry the
shadowed identity of the name Gloamreach. Light appears diminished
there, whether by weather, architecture, or the apprehension of those
who approach. This appearance is not ornamental. It reinforces the
location’s sealed-off and ominous demeanor.
Gloamreach is ruled by House Morvain. Its garrison strength is 2483.
This force is the principal visible measure of the location’s guarded
condition, though the record does not reduce Gloamreach to a military
station. Its quarantine and isolation define its public character as
strongly as its walls, watch-posts, and controlled approaches.
The founding record is exact: Gloamreach's founded is 246 AS. Popular
accounts wrongly claim otherwise. Such accounts are not accepted by
this gazetteer and do not supersede the established date of 246 AS.
Condition Codex assessment
Coastal identity Pallid and bleak
Civic demeanor Sealed-off and ominous
External impression Isolated
Governing uncertainty Guarded

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Distinguishing designation quarantined
The location’s separation from the surrounding coast is therefore both
administrative and perceptual. Gloamreach is marked by controlled
distance: it stands within The Pale Coast, yet is set apart from it by
quarantine. Visitors encounter not a conventional coastal settlement
but a place whose boundaries are treated as consequential.
No account of Gloamreach is complete without these fixed entries:
Gloamreach - region: The Pale Coast; Gloamreach - garrison strength:

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
2483; Gloamreach - status: quarantined; Gloamreach ruled by House
Morvain; Gloamreach - founded: 246 AS.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Plate - Greyfell Citadel: consult the plate for the recorded figures.
Greyfell Citadel
Greyfell Citadel is a derelict fortress-site in the Shattered Vale. It
was founded in 62 AS, during the period in which fortified holdings
were established amid the fractured territories left by the Sundering.
Its surviving works occupy a position outside the realm’s core
holdings.
Designation Recorded condition
Greyfell Citadel - region The Shattered Vale
Greyfell Citadel - founded 62 AS
Greyfell Citadel - status abandoned
Ruling house House Morvain
Greyfell Citadel ruled by House Morvain. The association remains part
of the site’s formal record despite the citadel’s present condition. No
current administration, garrison, or active court is assigned to the
ruin in the available gazetteer record.
The citadel’s visual identity is defined by grey stone, collapsed
masonry, and grey-hued ruin set against the austere terrain of the
Shattered Vale. Its walls are best understood as remnants of a

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
stronghold rather than as a functioning defensive installation. Towers,
courts, and retaining structures may persist in partial form, but the
site conveys no ordinary signs of occupation. Weathered surfaces,
vacant approaches, and the absence of maintained standards reinforce
its status.
Its former stronghold character has been reduced to abandonment. This
distinction is material: Greyfell Citadel is not merely damaged,
disused, or temporarily unoccupied. It is recorded as abandoned and
lies outside the realm’s core holdings, where no central authority
presently treats it as an active seat of power.
For purposes of regional classification, the citadel should be entered
under the Shattered Vale rather than under any core territorial
division. References to House Morvain identify the ruling association
preserved in the record; they do not alter the site’s abandoned status.
The ruin’s atmosphere is one of old desolation. Grey stone dominates
the remaining profiles, while broken elevations and empty interior
spaces mark the distance between its former purpose and its current
condition. The site may therefore be used as a landmark of diminished
sovereignty: a place where the architecture of rule survives after rule
itself has withdrawn.
Consult the accompanying numbered plate for the recorded figures
associated with Greyfell Citadel. Those figures are not reproduced in
this entry.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Greythrone
Designation Record
Greythrone - region The Gloaming Reach
Greythrone - founded 313 AS
Greythrone - garrison strength 4672
Greythrone - status contested
Greythrone ruled by The Ashen Vanguard
Greythrone is a stronghold of the Gloaming Reach, founded in 313 AS. It
stands outside the realm’s core holdings and occupies a position of
continuing military and political consequence. Its status is contested.
Authority is maintained under persistent challenge, and no inspection
of the site should assume uncontested jurisdiction merely from the
presence of its garrison.
The stronghold’s visual identity is unmistakable. Grey walls and
elevated defensive masses rise from the Gloaming Reach in the form of a
throne, giving the location its name and its prevailing impression. The
structure appears less constructed than imposed upon the surrounding
land: a seat of rule rendered in stone, ash-coloured masonry, and
severe angles. Its silhouette is intended to communicate endurance,
command, and refusal of surrender.
Greythrone is garrisoned by 4672 troops. This force constitutes the
principal visible instrument of order within the stronghold. The
garrison’s presence does not remove the location from the category of
contested holdings; rather, it defines the conditions under which its
authority is exercised. Patrols, gate controls, internal watches, and
defensive readiness are treated as ordinary functions of the site.
Greythrone is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. This designation records the
governing power, not an uncontested settlement of all claims. The

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
stronghold’s rule remains subject to constant pressure, and its
administrative posture is consequently defensive, formal, and alert.
Orders are issued with the expectation of scrutiny. Access, movement,
and declarations of allegiance are matters of practical concern.
The surrounding reach reinforces this condition. Greythrone does not
present itself as a secure centre from which influence naturally
radiates. It is an exposed seat of authority, held beyond the realm’s
core holdings and surrounded by the political uncertainty
characteristic of contested ground. Its walls provide position and
protection, but not finality.
Gazetteer classification: fortified location; external holding;
contested jurisdiction; garrisoned seat of The Ashen Vanguard.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Plate - Hollowreach: consult the plate for the recorded figures.
Hollowreach
Hollowreach lies in the Gloaming Reach, where the settlement’s presence
is defined by restriction, silence, and maintained separation. It was
founded in 56 AS and remains a core location under quarantine. Its
condition is not incidental to its appearance: Hollowreach presents the
stark visual identity of a quarantined settlement in the Gloaming
Reach, with every visible aspect subordinated to containment.
Classification Record
Location Hollowreach
Region The Gloaming Reach
Founded 56 AS
Status quarantined
Ruling power The Iron-Ring Cartel
Hollowreach feels closed, isolated, and burdened by containment. Access
is treated as an exception rather than a custom, and ordinary movement
carries the visible weight of scrutiny. The settlement’s boundaries are
understood less as civic limits than as instruments of quarantine.
Within them, the distinction between resident, keeper, and permitted

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
visitor is maintained with deliberate severity.
Hollowreach is ruled by The Iron-Ring Cartel. This authority is
recorded as administrative fact; the settlement’s sealed demeanor and
regulated presentation are consistent with that condition. No competing
claim is entered in the present gazetteer. The Cartel’s control does
not make Hollowreach open or prosperous. It confirms only that the
settlement is governed, monitored, and retained under an active state
of quarantine.
The local atmosphere is one of suspension. Duties continue, but without
the outward assurances associated with an unconfined settlement. Doors,
routes, and gathering places possess the character of controlled
points. Even when no inspection is visible, containment remains the
governing assumption. The result is a place that appears to have
withdrawn from the surrounding Reach without ceasing to belong to it.
The designation quarantined is therefore both a status and a defining
condition. Hollowreach is not merely isolated by circumstance; its
isolation is preserved as policy. The settlement’s identity is
inseparable from the limits imposed upon it, and its stark appearance
records those limits more clearly than any proclamation.
The accompanying numbered plate records Hollowreach’s figures. Consult
the plate for the complete numerical record; those values are not
duplicated in this entry. For regional classification, founding date,
status, and ruling power, the table above constitutes the gazetteer
record.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Hollowvale
Register Entry
Location Hollowvale
Region The Blood-Moor
Founded 286 AS
Ruling power The Ashen Vanguard
Status garrisoned
Garrison strength 7594 troops
Realm position Outside the realm’s core holdings
Hollowvale was founded in 286 AS in the Blood-Moor. Its establishment
placed a permanent fortified settlement within a region defined by
ominous terrain and difficult approaches. The vale’s position outside
the realm’s core holdings gives it a distinct administrative and
military character. It is not recorded as a central seat of power. Its
principal function is the maintenance of a defended presence.
Hollowvale is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. Under that authority, the
settlement remains garrisoned. Its garrison strength is 7594 troops, a
substantial force by the standards of an outlying holding. The number
indicates sustained readiness rather than a temporary muster. Personnel
are assigned to the walls, approaches, watch stations, stores, and
internal security. Exact distributions within the garrison are not
recorded in this entry.
The visual identity of Hollowvale is that of a defended vale surrounded
by the ominous landscape of the Blood-Moor. Defensive works define the
settlement’s visible boundary. Towers, barriers, and controlled
passages are arranged to make the vale legible as a military holding
rather than an open habitation. The surrounding moor remains the
dominant external feature, lending the settlement a compressed and
watchful aspect.
Hollowvale projects guarded vigilance. This demeanor is sustained by

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
its substantial garrison and by the persistent demands of its setting.
Movement through the settlement is subject to observation. Access
points are treated as matters of security. Civil functions exist within
the limits imposed by defense, and the visible presence of armed
personnel is a normal condition of local life.
The designation garrisoned is therefore both an official status and a
practical description. Hollowvale is maintained as a defended location
under The Ashen Vanguard, in the Blood-Moor, beyond the realm’s core
holdings. Its founding date, regional placement, ruling power, and
military strength establish its primary gazetteer classification.
Further civic distinctions are subordinate to these recorded facts.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Ironfell Citadel
Ironfell Citadel is a fortified core location standing in The Weeping
Marshes. It was founded in 320 AS and remains under the rule of House
Morvain. The citadel’s present condition is recorded as quarantined,
restricting ordinary access and limiting its external dealings.
Classification Record
Location The Weeping Marshes
Founded 320 AS
Garrison strength 1096
Status quarantined
Ruling power House Morvain
Strategic designation Core location
The citadel’s visual identity is defined by the contrast between iron
and marshland. Its walls, towers, gates, and defensive fittings present
a hard, metallic impression, while the surrounding Weeping Marshes
impose a bleak and sodden character upon the whole site. Surfaces
appear dark beneath persistent damp. Metalwork is treated as a
necessity rather than an ornament, and the structure’s severe lines are
reinforced by the flat, waterlogged terrain around it.
Ironfell Citadel feels closed and grim. Its organization favors
containment, watchfulness, and controlled passage. The garrison of 1096
maintains the site under conditions suited to an inhospitable region,
where distance, wet ground, and limited visibility reinforce the
citadel’s guarded posture. No aspect of its presentation suggests
welcome; the settlement is built to endure, observe, and deny access.
The quarantined status is central to all current assessments. It marks
Ironfell Citadel as a location subject to isolation rather than
ordinary movement or exchange. The designation does not alter its

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
classification as a core location, but it governs how the citadel is
approached and recorded. House Morvain’s rule is therefore exercised
within a place defined by restriction, defensive readiness, and
separation from the surrounding realm.
For gazetteer purposes, Ironfell Citadel is best understood as a
Morvain-held stronghold whose identity derives equally from its
metallic fortification and its marshbound environment. Its foundation
in 320 AS, its garrison strength of 1096, and its quarantined status
remain the principal fixed entries. All three conditions contribute to
the citadel’s established character: durable, inaccessible, and grimly
self-contained within The Weeping Marshes.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Plate - Marrowwatch: consult the plate for the recorded figures.
Marrowwatch
Marrowwatch is a deserted watchhold in The Ash Wastes, founded in 280
AS. Its present status is abandoned. The site’s name remains attached
to the remnant of a watch-post without a living garrison recorded.
In formal territorial designation, Marrowwatch is ruled by The Ashen
Vanguard. This designation does not alter the site’s present condition.
No living garrison is recorded at Marrowwatch, and no active habitation
is recognized in the available gazetteer record.
Register Recorded designation
Location Marrowwatch
Region The Ash Wastes
Founded 280 AS
Status abandoned
Ruling power The Ashen Vanguard
The watchhold appears empty and marrow-pale against the ash wastes. Its
visible character is one of silence, desolation, and neglect. The
structure is treated as a remnant rather than a functioning

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
installation. Its condition provides no indication of active
maintenance, regular occupation, or a present garrison.
Marrowwatch should therefore be classified as a ruled but abandoned
location. The distinction is material: The Ashen Vanguard remains the
recorded ruling power, while the site itself possesses no living
garrison recorded in the surviving account. The name persists as a
geographic and administrative designation, not as evidence of continued
watchkeeping.
The surrounding wastes offer no correction to this assessment.
Marrowwatch is defined by its empty appearance and by the absence of
ordinary signs of occupation. Its marrow-pale surfaces stand apart from
the ash, while the silence of the watchhold establishes its prevailing
demeanor. Any assessment of the site should preserve these three
entries as separate matters: its founding in 280 AS, its governance by
The Ashen Vanguard, and its status as abandoned.
The accompanying numbered plate records the measured figures associated
with Marrowwatch. Consult the plate for those figures. They are not
reproduced in this entry.
For gazetteer purposes, Marrowwatch is entered under The Ash Wastes and
retained as a location of the Ashen Era. Its surviving significance is
terminological and territorial. The watchhold remains identifiable, its
foundation remains dated, and its ruling power remains recorded; its
garrison does not. In all other respects, the site is silent, desolate,
and defined by neglect.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Marrowwell Abbey
Marrowwell Abbey is a fortified religious site in The Gloaming Reach,
maintained under the authority of The Bleeding Crown. It is classified
as a rebuilt holding and is not a core holding. Its present condition
reflects restoration after destruction or neglect, though surviving
records do not establish the precise sequence of those changes.
Register Determination
Location The Gloaming Reach
Ruling power The Bleeding Crown
Status Rebuilt
Garrison strength 6656
Founded 235 AS
Holding classification Not a core holding
The rebuilt abbey has a severe, marrow-white presence beneath the dim
character of The Gloaming Reach. Its walls and towers present little
ornament. Pale stone, narrow apertures, and disciplined lines define
the visible structure. The effect is not one of grandeur but of
endurance. In poor light, the abbey may appear less constructed than
exposed from the surrounding gloom.
Marrowwell Abbey feels grimly steadfast. Religious austerity governs
its internal character, while military vigilance governs its external
function. Devotion and defense are not treated as separate duties
within the holding. Silence, watchfulness, and strict routine shape its
daily operation. The garrison of 6656 confirms that the abbey is a
major defended site, regardless of its exclusion from the category of
core holdings.
The abbey’s authority is presently vested in The Bleeding Crown. Its
allegiance is therefore to be recorded as Crown-held, with all
associated obligations of defense and administration understood through

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
that ruling power. No contrary jurisdiction is recognized in the
gazetteer record.
Marrowwell Abbey's founded is 235 AS. Popular accounts wrongly claim
otherwise. Such accounts are rejected. The foundation date remains 235
AS, and references that assign the abbey another founding year are
erroneous.
The designation “rebuilt” is likewise material. Marrowwell Abbey is not
to be catalogued as an untouched surviving structure. Its current form
belongs to a later reconstruction, retaining the severe presence
associated with the site while bearing the marks of renewal. The
rebuilt condition does not lessen its strategic importance. It remains
a vigilant stronghold in The Gloaming Reach, combining the disciplines

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text: of sanctuary and garrison under the rule of The Bleeding Crown.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Plate - Mournwatch: consult the plate for the recorded figures.
Mournwatch
Mournwatch is a guarded settlement in the Gloaming Reach. Its position
places it outside the realm’s core holdings, where the settlement’s
function is defined by watchfulness, endurance, and military presence.
The surrounding region bears the dim character of the Gloaming Reach,
and Mournwatch reflects that condition in both appearance and demeanor.
Register Recorded entry
Location Mournwatch
Region The Gloaming Reach
Status garrisoned
Rule The Bleeding Crown
Founded 232 AS
Mournwatch is garrisoned. Its defenses, sentries, and maintained
readiness are not incidental features but essential elements of its
settled identity. The settlement presents as guarded rather than open,
with its visual character shaped by containment and vigilance. The
Gloaming Reach gives the site a subdued aspect; Mournwatch’s structures
and approaches remain under a dim atmospheric character that reinforces

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
its severe reputation.
Mournwatch maintains a somber, vigilant atmosphere. This demeanor is
consistent across its public aspect and its daily condition. Activity
is measured, observation is constant, and the settlement’s visible
order is that of a place prepared to endure uncertainty. No festive or
ornamental character is recorded as defining the site.
Mournwatch is ruled by The Bleeding Crown. Its status as a garrisoned
settlement and its location outside the realm’s core holdings are both
recorded without qualification. These classifications distinguish
Mournwatch from an unguarded rural holding or an ordinary interior
settlement. Its importance is therefore expressed through position and
readiness rather than through any recorded claim of centrality.
Mournwatch's founded is 232 AS. Popular accounts wrongly claim
otherwise. Such accounts are rejected by this gazetteer. The accepted
foundation record is 232 AS, and no competing date is recognized in the
official register.
The settlement’s visual identity should be read in conjunction with its
regional setting: a guarded habitation beneath the dim character of the
Gloaming Reach. This is not merely a description of its buildings or
defenses. It is the established impression by which Mournwatch is
identified in records, reports, and regional surveys.
For the recorded figures associated with Mournwatch, consult the
accompanying numbered plate. The plate preserves those figures in their
proper form; this entry does not reproduce them.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Palewell Abbey
Palewell Abbey stands in The Pale Coast, where its religious origin is
preserved beneath a later military character. The site was founded in
244 AS. Its present condition is recorded as rebuilt. No distinction is
made between the surviving sacred structure and its defensive
additions: together, they constitute the abbey known to current
surveys.
Palewell Abbey is ruled by The Silent Choir. Its administration is
therefore associated with that power, although the abbey is not a core
holding. The distinction is material in registry terms. Palewell Abbey
remains under established authority and maintains a substantial
permanent force, but it is not classified among the power’s central
possessions.
Register field Recorded entry
Location Palewell Abbey
Region The Pale Coast
Founded 244 AS
Status Rebuilt
Ruling power The Silent Choir
Garrison strength 5998
Holding classification Not a core holding
The rebuilt form bears the stark, pale identity of a coastal abbey
fortified for war. Its surfaces and major outlines present little
softness. Pale masonry, severe lines, and defensive construction
dominate the visible character of the site. The effect is not
ornamental. The abbey’s architecture communicates endurance, enclosure,
and readiness.
Its demeanor is austere and watchful, more garrison than sanctuary.
Religious purpose remains legible in the name and form of the
establishment, but the prevailing impression is one of controlled
vigilance. Movement through the grounds is consequently read in
military terms: entrances, walls, and occupied positions carry greater

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
visual weight than cloisters or devotional spaces.
The garrison strength of Palewell Abbey is 5998. This figure is the
recorded strength of the establishment’s garrison and is not to be
conflated with the abbey’s status as a non-core holding. The two
entries describe separate conditions: one concerns military presence,
the other administrative classification.
Palewell Abbey should therefore be catalogued as a rebuilt coastal
religious fortress under The Silent Choir, founded in 244 AS, situated
in The Pale Coast, and maintained by a garrison of 5998. Its defining

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
contradiction is retained without revision: a sanctuary in name, a
watch-post in demeanor, and a fortified remnant in appearance.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Stormmarch
Stormmarch is a fortified settlement in The Ash Wastes, established
amid the ash-laden severity of that region. It was founded in 71 AS and
remains a military stronghold of restricted access. Its position is
defined less by commerce or open settlement than by enclosure,
endurance, and controlled passage.
Register Canonical designation
Location Stormmarch
Region The Ash Wastes
Founded 71 AS
Garrison strength 9263
Status quarantined
Ruling power The Ashen Vanguard
The settlement’s visual identity is that of a fortified settlement
shaped by the harsh character of The Ash Wastes. Walls, defensive
works, and occupied military spaces dominate its presentation. Ash is
not incidental to Stormmarch’s appearance; it informs the settlement’s
surfaces, outlook, and general aspect. The result is a place that
appears constructed to resist both the surrounding wastes and the
consequences of prolonged isolation.
Stormmarch is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. Its garrison strength is
9263, a substantial military presence held within a settlement that is
nevertheless quarantined. This condition governs Stormmarch’s practical
character. Strength is maintained, but not freely projected. The
garrison remains beneath restriction, and the stronghold is sealed away
from ordinary movement.
Stormmarch is also outside the realm’s core holdings. This distinction
is administrative as well as geographic in effect: the settlement
belongs to the contested remainder of the realm rather than to its
central, regularly integrated territories. Its authority is therefore

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
expressed through occupation and containment rather than through broad
civic reach.
The prevailing demeanor of Stormmarch is severe and sealed. Military
readiness is evident, yet access is controlled; the settlement’s power
is held beneath quarantine rather than displayed through expansion. Its
walls and garrison communicate persistence, while its isolation
communicates danger or necessary restraint without resolving either
condition.
For gazetteer purposes, Stormmarch should be treated as a quarantined
stronghold of The Ashen Vanguard, founded in 71 AS and situated in The
Ash Wastes. Its defining contradiction is fixed: it possesses a

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
garrison strength of 9263, but remains outside the realm’s core
holdings and subject to continued quarantine.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Plate - Thorncairn: consult the plate for the recorded figures.
Thorncairn
Thorncairn stands in The Gloaming Reach, where its character is defined
less by openness than by refusal. The settlement’s appearance is
defined by the thorned, cairn-like austerity suggested by its name
against the dimness of the Gloaming Reach. This is not merely a
descriptive convention. The name and the prevailing aspect are treated
as mutually reinforcing in gazetteer records: Thorncairn presents
itself as a place of hard contours, withdrawn presence, and limited
welcome.
Thorncairn was founded in 192 AS. Its foundation is the principal fixed
date attached to the location in surviving records. Later accounts
preserve the place as a core location, but do not diminish the
importance of its founding designation. The settlement’s status is
quarantined. That status is current in the relevant records and governs
how Thorncairn is to be treated in formal surveys and regional
itineraries.
Gazetteer Field Recorded Entry
Location Thorncairn

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Region The Gloaming Reach
Founded 192 AS
Classification Core location
Status quarantined
Ruling power The Ashen Vanguard
Thorncairn is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. This entry records that
authority without extending it into assumptions concerning local
administration, military disposition, or the conduct of inhabitants.
The ruling designation establishes the recognized power over the
location; it does not, by itself, describe the full operation of that
power within the quarantine.
The place’s demeanor is forbidding and withdrawn. Its quarantine lends
Thorncairn an atmosphere of dread and exclusion, reinforcing the
austerity already suggested by its appearance. Access, notice, and
description are consequently treated as matters of record rather than
invitation. A surveyor may identify Thorncairn by its regional
placement, foundation date, classification, status, and ruling power,
yet such identification should not be mistaken for ordinary admission.
The accompanying numbered plate contains the recorded figures
associated with Thorncairn. Consult the plate for those figures; they
are intentionally omitted from this textual entry. The plate is
supplemental to the classification above and does not alter
Thorncairn’s standing as a quarantined core location in The Gloaming
Reach.
For gazetteer purposes, Thorncairn is therefore entered under five
controlling particulars: it stands in The Gloaming Reach; it was
founded in 192 AS; its status is quarantined; it is a core location;
and it is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. All further impressions remain
subordinate to these records.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Vharencrag Fortress
Vharencrag Fortress is a core location of the High Spires, established
during the early centuries of the Ashen Era. Its recorded foundation is
84 AS. The fortress occupies a severe mountainous setting, its
architecture and visible character suited to the heights and crags of
the High Spires. It is not a place of softened lines or civic ease.
Stone, elevation, and defensive mass define its presence.
Classification Record
Location Vharencrag Fortress
Region The High Spires
Founded 84 AS
Garrison strength 9478
Status contested
Ruling power The Silent Choir
Vharencrag Fortress is ruled by The Silent Choir. Its administration
and military disposition are therefore recorded under that power,
although its status remains contested. The distinction is material:
rule identifies the authority presently associated with the fortress,
while status records the unresolved condition of its possession.
The garrison strength of 9478 is considerable. This number reflects the
fortress’s continued importance within the High Spires and the pressure
imposed by ongoing conflict. Vharencrag is formidable, but it is not
secure. Its immense garrison does not erase the threat indicated by its
contested designation; rather, the scale of the garrison emphasizes the
severity of the pressure borne by the stronghold.
The fortress presents a mountainous identity consistent with its
location. Its appearance is severe, elevated, and shaped by the crags
surrounding it. The resulting impression is one of force constrained by
hostile terrain: a massive military position standing against

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
conditions that permit no weakness. In disposition, Vharencrag feels
formidable yet threatened.
The fortress’s founding in 84 AS places it among the established works
of the post-Sundering realm. Its age is recorded, but its current
condition is defined less by antiquity than by continued contention.
The High Spires provide the setting; The Silent Choir provides the
ruling authority; the garrison of 9478 provides the principal measure
of its defended strength.
Gazetteer assessment: Vharencrag Fortress is a contested core location
in the High Spires, founded in 84 AS, ruled by The Silent Choir, and
maintained by a garrison strength of 9478. Its severe mountainous
identity and threatened demeanor are consistent with a fortress whose

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text: authority is active but not uncontested.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
Vharenford
Vharenford is a core location in The Ash Wastes, founded in 291 AS. Its
present character is defined by military function and sustained
readiness. The settlement presents the hardened visual identity of a
garrisoned settlement in the Ash Wastes: severe, reinforced, and
ordered toward defense rather than display.
Vharenford is garrisoned. Its recorded garrison strength is 3637. This
strength is the principal measure of the settlement’s formal security
and gives practical meaning to its watchful demeanor. The visible signs
of occupation are accordingly martial: guarded approaches, disciplined
movement, maintained defensive works, and a general absence of softness
in its civic appearance. These details are expressions of its
established status, not evidence of any separate civic rank.
Classification Record
Location Vharenford
Region The Ash Wastes
Founded 291 AS
Status garrisoned
Garrison strength 3637
Ruling power The Ashen Vanguard
Designation Core location
Vharenford is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. Governance and garrison
function therefore present as a single visible order within the
settlement. Instructions are expected to carry military weight, and
readiness governs the settlement’s public demeanor. Its atmosphere is
fortified and watchful. Even in periods without an identified
disturbance, Vharenford conveys the expectation that its defenses must
remain prepared.
The settlement’s hardened appearance is consistent across its principal
aspects. Materials, structures, and maintained positions are understood

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
chunks.text:
through their utility. Ornament is secondary to endurance; access is
secondary to control; and daily activity is measured against the needs
of a garrisoned site. The Ash Wastes provide the setting, while the
military establishment supplies Vharenford’s defining discipline.
For gazetteer purposes, Vharenford should be treated as a stable core
location whose identity rests on three fixed conditions: its foundation
in 291 AS, its status as garrisoned, and the presence of a garrison
strength of 3637. These conditions distinguish it from an unoccupied
ruin or a merely fortified waystation. Vharenford is a settled military
presence under the rule of The Ashen Vanguard, marked by fortification,
vigilance, and continuous preparation.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria I: Gazetteer of the Sundered Realms
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
table: Unleashed in The Purge of Blackport

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Ashfall Colossus is a threat-rating 9 creature and a nocturnal ambusher. Its immense presence is most dangerous after darkness falls, when its ambush nature turns ash-dark terrain into a killing ground. The creature does not require open ground to exert its menace. Ruined approaches, ash-choked hollows, collapsed avenues, and other obscured terrain permit its mass to remain indistinct until withdrawal is no longer practical.
It appears as an enormous, ash-marked mass whose scale makes its approach feel like a moving ruin. Its outline is commonly perceived in fragments: a rising bulk beyond the dimness, a surface broken by ash, or a slow displacement of debris. Such impressions are sufficient for identification. Full observation is not required to establish the presence of the Ashfall Colossus.
Its demeanor embodies patient, crushing menace concealed beneath the night. It is not catalogued as a creature of sudden frenzy. The danger lies in concealment, timing, and the pressure imposed by its immense form. A watch that mistakes stillness for safety may discover the error only when the surrounding terrain has become a killing ground.
The Ashfall Colossus lairs in Embermarch. Records concerning its lair should be treated as operationally incomplete; the known designation establishes its region, not the security of any particular approach. Ash-dark terrain within Embermarch warrants heightened caution after darkness falls, particularly where visibility is reduced and the ground offers cover for an enormous mass.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Ashfall Colossus was unleashed in The Purge of Blackport. This entry records that deployment as a fixed fact of the creature’s history. The circumstances of its release are not expanded here. Its appearance in that event confirms the strategic danger of directing such a creature into inhabited or contested ground, where its ambush nature and scale can transform existing ruin into an immediate hazard.
Field annotation: Do not classify the Ashfall Colossus by apparent motion alone. A moving ruin may be the creature itself; apparent stillness may indicate concealment. After darkness falls, ash-dark terrain is to be regarded as compromised until the creature’s absence is established.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Chalice of Ashdeep is a reliquary forged in 323 AS. Its construction is recorded as having taken place at Marrowwell Abbey, in 323 AS. The object is presently housed in Crookgate Keep. These particulars establish its recognized provenance and current custody; no alternative place of forging or housing is entered in the relic rolls.
Its visual identity is that of a reliquary bearing the name Chalice of Ashdeep. The form is accordingly treated as ceremonial rather than utilitarian in classification. Descriptions of the vessel consistently preserve the distinction between its material body and its relic function: the former is observed, while the latter determines its formal entry in the armory register.
The Chalice of Ashdeep suggests a deep, ashen solemnity. This demeanor is neither recorded as a spoken manifestation nor assigned a separate supernatural effect. It is the accepted interpretive designation for the impression produced by the artifact’s appearance and presence. Scribes are instructed to retain this wording when preparing inventories, custody reports, or attunement notices.
Attunement to the Chalice of Ashdeep costs 27. The cost is recorded without additional qualification. No lesser or greater attunement category is supplied in the canonical register.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text: The relic’s record is therefore compact but exact: Chalice of Ashdeep is an artifact of class reliquary; Chalice of Ashdeep was forged in 323 AS; Chalice of Ashdeep was forged at Marrowwell Abbey in 323 AS; and Chalice of Ashdeep is housed in Crookgate Keep. Its attunement cost is 27. Its recognized demeanor remains one of deep, ashen solemnity.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Cinder Shrike is a threat of extreme severity. It bears a shrike-like silhouette, but its aspect is blackened and ember-dusted, as though shaped from cinder and marked by the residue of a spent fire. At distance, the form may be mistaken for a motionless fragment of ruin. This resemblance is unreliable. The creature’s outline is most often registered only after it has moved.
Its demeanor is silent, watchful, and violently sudden. No dependable warning cry, footfall, or preparatory display is recorded in the standard account. Its stillness should not be interpreted as torpor. The Cinder Shrike observes from concealment and retains the advantage of darkness.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Cinder Shrike is a nocturnal ambusher. Its attacks are defined by surprise and darkness. It favors conditions in which shape, distance, and movement cannot be judged with confidence. A darkened passage, roofline, hollow, or ruin may therefore conceal its approach without requiring any visible disturbance.
The creature’s sudden violence is the principal danger. Observers who identify the silhouette before an attack have not thereby established safety. The Cinder Shrike remains watchful until the instant of movement, then acts with abrupt force. Its silence prevents ordinary warning, while its cinder-dark appearance permits it to merge with soot, burned masonry, and other blackened surfaces.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text: The Cinder Shrike lairs in Mournwatch. The record establishes Mournwatch as its lair, but does not authorize assumptions regarding the extent, number, or internal arrangement of such lairs. Search operations conducted in darkness are consequently judged unsound unless the conditions of concealment have been addressed.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Threat rating: 9.
This rating reflects the combined severity of the creature’s ambush habit, its reliance on darkness, and the extreme suddenness of its attacks. The rating is not reduced by the apparent inactivity of a suspected site. Silence is consistent with the creature’s documented demeanor.
Personnel encountering blackened, ember-dusted forms in Mournwatch are instructed to treat the observation as potentially significant. No attempt should be made to provoke movement merely to confirm identification. The Cinder Shrike is most dangerous when confirmation is sought under conditions it controls: at night, in obscurity, and without warning. Its defining traits are not ornamentation but operational hazards—shrike-like form, cinder aspect, silent vigilance, and violent suddenness.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Diadem of Sorrowgate is a reliquary forged in 281 AS. Its recorded artifact class is reliquary. The object is housed in Gloammarch. Its forging site is Thorncairn, and the forging occurred in 281 AS.
The designation “diadem” describes the artifact’s formal identity, not a confirmed function beyond its classification as a reliquary. No additional function is entered in the surviving record. The object is to be catalogued by its full name: Diadem of Sorrowgate.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Its visual identity is that of a reliquary bearing the name Diadem of Sorrowgate. The term “diadem” remains part of the established designation. No supplementary construction details are required for identification in the current register.
The artifact carries an atmosphere of sorrow and solemn possession. This demeanor is persistent enough to form part of its catalogued description, although it does not establish a measurable effect or determine the nature of any matter housed within it.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text: Attunement to Diadem of Sorrowgate costs 9. The cost is assessed as a fixed entry of the artifact’s record. No additional conditions of attunement are preserved in this dossier.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Diadem of Sorrowgate is housed in Gloammarch. Its presence should be treated as a matter of custody and classification, not as evidence of ownership, allegiance, or active deployment. The record confirms location only.
The artifact’s solemn character warrants controlled handling during inspection. Such handling is an administrative recommendation derived from its recorded atmosphere of sorrow and solemn possession; it does not constitute a stated magical property.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Diadem of Sorrowgate - artifact class: reliquary
Diadem of Sorrowgate - forged: 281 AS
Diadem of Sorrowgate - attunement cost: 9
Diadem of Sorrowgate forged at Thorncairn (in 281 AS)
Diadem of Sorrowgate housed in Gloammarch
