chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Ashfall Colossus
Classification Record
Name Ashfall Colossus
Type Creature
Threat rating 9
Habit Nocturnal ambusher
Lair Embermarch
Recorded deployment Unleashed in The Purge of Blackport
The Ashfall Colossus is a threat-rating 9 creature and a nocturnal
ambusher. Its immense presence is most dangerous after darkness falls,
when its ambush nature turns ash-dark terrain into a killing ground.
The creature does not require open ground to exert its menace. Ruined
approaches, ash-choked hollows, collapsed avenues, and other obscured
terrain permit its mass to remain indistinct until withdrawal is no
longer practical.
It appears as an enormous, ash-marked mass whose scale makes its
approach feel like a moving ruin. Its outline is commonly perceived in
fragments: a rising bulk beyond the dimness, a surface broken by ash,
or a slow displacement of debris. Such impressions are sufficient for
identification. Full observation is not required to establish the
presence of the Ashfall Colossus.
Its demeanor embodies patient, crushing menace concealed beneath the
night. It is not catalogued as a creature of sudden frenzy. The danger
lies in concealment, timing, and the pressure imposed by its immense
form. A watch that mistakes stillness for safety may discover the error
only when the surrounding terrain has become a killing ground.
The Ashfall Colossus lairs in Embermarch. Records concerning its lair
should be treated as operationally incomplete; the known designation
establishes its region, not the security of any particular approach.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Ash-dark terrain within Embermarch warrants heightened caution after
darkness falls, particularly where visibility is reduced and the ground
offers cover for an enormous mass.
The Ashfall Colossus was unleashed in The Purge of Blackport. This
entry records that deployment as a fixed fact of the creature’s
history. The circumstances of its release are not expanded here. Its
appearance in that event confirms the strategic danger of directing
such a creature into inhabited or contested ground, where its ambush
nature and scale can transform existing ruin into an immediate hazard.
Field annotation: Do not classify the Ashfall Colossus by apparent
motion alone. A moving ruin may be the creature itself; apparent
stillness may indicate concealment. After darkness falls, ash-dark

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
table: Unleashed in The Purge of Blackport

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
terrain is to be regarded as compromised until the creature’s absence
is established.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Chalice of Ashdeep
Classification Record
Name Chalice of Ashdeep
Artifact class Reliquary
Forged 323 AS
Place of forging Marrowwell Abbey
Attunement cost 27
Present housing Crookgate Keep
The Chalice of Ashdeep is a reliquary forged in 323 AS. Its
construction is recorded as having taken place at Marrowwell Abbey, in
323 AS. The object is presently housed in Crookgate Keep. These
particulars establish its recognized provenance and current custody; no
alternative place of forging or housing is entered in the relic rolls.
Its visual identity is that of a reliquary bearing the name Chalice of
Ashdeep. The form is accordingly treated as ceremonial rather than
utilitarian in classification. Descriptions of the vessel consistently
preserve the distinction between its material body and its relic
function: the former is observed, while the latter determines its
formal entry in the armory register.
The Chalice of Ashdeep suggests a deep, ashen solemnity. This demeanor
is neither recorded as a spoken manifestation nor assigned a separate
supernatural effect. It is the accepted interpretive designation for
the impression produced by the artifact’s appearance and presence.
Scribes are instructed to retain this wording when preparing
inventories, custody reports, or attunement notices.
Attunement to the Chalice of Ashdeep costs 27. The cost is recorded
without additional qualification. No lesser or greater attunement
category is supplied in the canonical register.
Custodial Note Entry
Current location Crookgate Keep
Required identification Chalice of Ashdeep
Attunement cost 27

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Registered origin Marrowwell Abbey
Registered forging year 323 AS
The relic’s record is therefore compact but exact: Chalice of Ashdeep
is an artifact of class reliquary; Chalice of Ashdeep was forged in 323
AS; Chalice of Ashdeep was forged at Marrowwell Abbey in 323 AS; and
Chalice of Ashdeep is housed in Crookgate Keep. Its attunement cost is
27. Its recognized demeanor remains one of deep, ashen solemnity.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Cinder Shrike
Classification Record
Name Cinder Shrike
Nature Creature
Threat rating 9
Habit nocturnal ambusher
Lair Mournwatch
Identification
The Cinder Shrike is a threat of extreme severity. It bears a
shrike-like silhouette, but its aspect is blackened and ember-dusted,
as though shaped from cinder and marked by the residue of a spent fire.
At distance, the form may be mistaken for a motionless fragment of
ruin. This resemblance is unreliable. The creature’s outline is most
often registered only after it has moved.
Its demeanor is silent, watchful, and violently sudden. No dependable
warning cry, footfall, or preparatory display is recorded in the
standard account. Its stillness should not be interpreted as torpor.
The Cinder Shrike observes from concealment and retains the advantage
of darkness.
Conduct
The Cinder Shrike is a nocturnal ambusher. Its attacks are defined by
surprise and darkness. It favors conditions in which shape, distance,
and movement cannot be judged with confidence. A darkened passage,
roofline, hollow, or ruin may therefore conceal its approach without
requiring any visible disturbance.
The creature’s sudden violence is the principal danger. Observers who
identify the silhouette before an attack have not thereby established
safety. The Cinder Shrike remains watchful until the instant of
movement, then acts with abrupt force. Its silence prevents ordinary
warning, while its cinder-dark appearance permits it to merge with
soot, burned masonry, and other blackened surfaces.
Range Record
The Cinder Shrike lairs in Mournwatch. The record establishes

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Mournwatch as its lair, but does not authorize assumptions regarding
the extent, number, or internal arrangement of such lairs. Search
operations conducted in darkness are consequently judged unsound unless
the conditions of concealment have been addressed.
Threat Assessment
Threat rating: 9.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
This rating reflects the combined severity of the creature’s ambush
habit, its reliance on darkness, and the extreme suddenness of its
attacks. The rating is not reduced by the apparent inactivity of a
suspected site. Silence is consistent with the creature’s documented
demeanor.
Personnel encountering blackened, ember-dusted forms in Mournwatch are
instructed to treat the observation as potentially significant. No
attempt should be made to provoke movement merely to confirm
identification. The Cinder Shrike is most dangerous when confirmation
is sought under conditions it controls: at night, in obscurity, and
without warning. Its defining traits are not ornamentation but
operational hazards—shrike-like form, cinder aspect, silent vigilance,
and violent suddenness.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Diadem of Sorrowgate
Classification Record
Name Diadem of Sorrowgate
Artifact class reliquary
Forged 281 AS
Forging site Thorncairn
Present housing Gloammarch
Attunement cost 9
Identification
Diadem of Sorrowgate is a reliquary forged in 281 AS. Its recorded
artifact class is reliquary. The object is housed in Gloammarch. Its
forging site is Thorncairn, and the forging occurred in 281 AS.
The designation “diadem” describes the artifact’s formal identity, not
a confirmed function beyond its classification as a reliquary. No
additional function is entered in the surviving record. The object is
to be catalogued by its full name: Diadem of Sorrowgate.
Appearance
Its visual identity is that of a reliquary bearing the name Diadem of
Sorrowgate. The term “diadem” remains part of the established
designation. No supplementary construction details are required for
identification in the current register.
The artifact carries an atmosphere of sorrow and solemn possession.
This demeanor is persistent enough to form part of its catalogued
description, although it does not establish a measurable effect or
determine the nature of any matter housed within it.
Attunement
Attunement to Diadem of Sorrowgate costs 9. The cost is assessed as a
fixed entry of the artifact’s record. No additional conditions of
attunement are preserved in this dossier.
Attunement Register Value
Cost 9
Recorded limitation None entered
Recorded benefit None entered
Custodial Note
Diadem of Sorrowgate is housed in Gloammarch. Its presence should be
treated as a matter of custody and classification, not as evidence of

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text: ownership, allegiance, or active deployment. The record confirms

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
location only.
The artifact’s solemn character warrants controlled handling during
inspection. Such handling is an administrative recommendation derived
from its recorded atmosphere of sorrow and solemn possession; it does
not constitute a stated magical property.
Summary
- Diadem of Sorrowgate - artifact class: reliquary
- Diadem of Sorrowgate - forged: 281 AS
- Diadem of Sorrowgate - attunement cost: 9
- Diadem of Sorrowgate forged at Thorncairn (in 281 AS)
- Diadem of Sorrowgate housed in Gloammarch

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Edge of Gloamreach
Volume: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Classification
Field Record
Name Edge of Gloamreach
Artifact class Grimoire
Attunement cost 46
Forged 303 AS
Place of forging Blackford
Current housing Blackford
Description
Edge of Gloamreach is a grimoire whose visual identity is defined by
the name Edge of Gloamreach borne upon it. Its presentation suggests a
shadowed, twilight-bound atmosphere. The impression is one of
diminished light and enclosed secrecy, though the artifact’s
classification remains strictly that of a grimoire.
The recorded attunement cost of Edge of Gloamreach is 46. This value is
to be treated as an established requirement for formal attunement. No
alternate cost is recognized in this codex.
Provenance
Edge of Gloamreach was forged at Blackford. The authoritative forging
record states that Edge of Gloamreach - forged: 303 AS. It is likewise
recorded that Edge of Gloamreach is housed in Blackford.
Edge of Gloamreach’s forged is 303 AS. Popular accounts wrongly claim
otherwise. Such accounts possess no standing against the established
record and are not to be used when dating the artifact, assigning it to
a period, or assessing its provenance.
Registry Note
The artifact’s name, class, attunement cost, place of forging, housing,
and forging year are the controlling entries:
- Edge of Gloamreach - artifact class: grimoire
- Edge of Gloamreach - attunement cost: 46
- Edge of Gloamreach forged at Blackford
- Edge of Gloamreach housed in Blackford
- Edge of Gloamreach - forged: 303 AS

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The designation “Edge” is part of the artifact’s proper name and does
not alter its classification. No weapon category is implied by the

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
designation. Likewise, the twilight-bound demeanor is a descriptive
assessment of its visual identity and atmosphere, not a separate
registry class.
Until a superior record supersedes the Blackford registry, Edge of
Gloamreach is to be catalogued as a grimoire forged in 303 AS at
Blackford, housed in Blackford, and requiring an attunement cost of 46.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Gauntlet of Sorrowfell
Artifact Class: Regalia Attunement Cost: 12 Forged: 391 AS Forging
Site: Vharencrag Fortress Current Repository: Greyfell Citadel
The Gauntlet of Sorrowfell is regalia of severe aspect, recognized by
its formal bearing and its atmosphere of sorrow and grim authority. Its
visual identity is that of regalia bearing the name Gauntlet of
Sorrowfell. No ornamental interpretation supersedes this designation;
the artifact is catalogued under its full and exact name.
Classification Record
Name Gauntlet of Sorrowfell
Artifact class regalia
Attunement cost 12
Forged 391 AS
Forged at Vharencrag Fortress
Housed in Greyfell Citadel
The Gauntlet of Sorrowfell was forged at Vharencrag Fortress and is
housed in Greyfell Citadel. These locations are fixed entries in the
armory register. The repository designation does not alter the
artifact’s class, and the forging site does not constitute a separate
title or variant.
The attunement cost of the Gauntlet of Sorrowfell is 12. This cost is
recorded without qualification. Prospective handlers are therefore to
consult the applicable regalia protocols before attempting attunement.
The artifact’s sorrowful demeanor is likewise an identifying
characteristic, not a supplemental epithet.
The authoritative record states plainly: Gauntlet of Sorrowfell's
forged is 391 AS. Popular accounts wrongly claim otherwise. Such
accounts are rejected. The accepted forging date is 391 AS, and no
competing date has standing in this codex.
The supplied record gives no further verified particulars concerning

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
the Gauntlet of Sorrowfell’s construction, prior bearers, powers, or
ceremonial employment. Accordingly, none are entered here as fact. Its
status remains defined by the following established particulars:
Gauntlet of Sorrowfell - artifact class: regalia; Gauntlet of
Sorrowfell - attunement cost: 12; Gauntlet of Sorrowfell forged at
Vharencrag Fortress; Gauntlet of Sorrowfell housed in Greyfell Citadel;
and Gauntlet of Sorrowfell - forged: 391 AS.
In all inventories, custody ledgers, and attunement schedules, the
exact name Gauntlet of Sorrowfell is to be retained. Variations based
on popular accounts are non-authoritative.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Gravemaw Wyrm
Classification Entry
Creature Gravemaw Wyrm
Threat rating 8
Habit sky hunter
Lair Marrowwell Abbey
Primary domain Open sky
Association Grave
The Gravemaw Wyrm is a grave-associated predator of exceptional aerial
dominance. Gravemaw Wyrm - threat rating: 8. Its presence converts the
open sky into a zone of immediate peril wherever it ranges. The
creature does not require concealment to establish danger; its command
of the air is itself sufficient.
Gravemaw Wyrm - habit: sky hunter. This designation is literal. The
wyrm is adapted to hunting through the sky, where its vast body and
pronounced maw form a silhouette suited to pursuit, descent, and
capture. The visible outline is not merely imposing. It is the defining
warning of a predator built to be recognized only after escape has
become doubtful.
Morphology
The Gravemaw Wyrm possesses a vast wyrm-like form. Its maw is
pronounced, giving the head a grave-devouring aspect even when viewed
at distance. The body presents as a continuous hunting shape rather
than a creature designed for concealment. Its silhouette is built for
hunting through the sky, with the proportions of an aerial predator
plainly expressed.
No ornamental interpretation is required. The association with death is
inherent to its form and conduct.
Demeanor
The Gravemaw Wyrm is relentlessly predatory. It carries the cold
inevitability of death from above, and its approach should be treated
as a direct escalation of danger rather than as a passing atmospheric
disturbance. Reports that describe it as patient, curious, or

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
territorial are insufficient classifications; the established demeanor
is relentless predation.
Lair Record
Gravemaw Wyrm lairs in Marrowwell Abbey. The site is therefore recorded
as a lair, not merely as a sighting ground or occasional refuge. Any
approach beneath the open sky must account for the possibility of

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
aerial threat. The presence of the lair does not lessen the creature’s
mobility; it identifies the point from which its range is maintained.
Field Assessment
Avoid exposure where concealment is unavailable. Do not mistake
distance for safety. The wyrm’s principal advantage is vertical
dominance, and its grave-associated nature should be considered a
reliable indicator of its threat profile. Under codex classification,
the Gravemaw Wyrm is not a lesser sky predator or a regional nuisance.
It is a threat-rating 8 creature whose hunting domain is the air
itself.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Lantern Moth Swarm
Classification Record
Name Lantern Moth Swarm
Nature Creature
Threat rating 6
Habit Siege-breaker
Lair Ashreach
Recorded deployment Unleashed in The Leaden Accord
The Lantern Moth Swarm is a siege-breaker of serious threat. It
operates as a collective rather than as a singular beast, bringing
mothlike disruption against fortified positions. Its presence is best
understood as an environmental assault: a dense cloud of moths occupies
the air, the approaches, and the immediate visual field of those within
the affected position.
The swarm carries the eerie visual impression of lantern-light. This
appearance is not to be treated as a calm illumination. It is a
shifting, obscuring radiance produced by the massed insects, rendering
the cloud difficult to read and its boundaries difficult to determine.
The effect is especially severe when the swarm presses against walls,
gates, towers, or other fortified positions.
Its demeanor is restless, overwhelming, and difficult to escape. The
collective does not present the measured movement of a disciplined
formation. It gathers, breaks, reforms, and presses onward as a single
disruptive presence. Observers should not assume that dispersal of one
portion signifies the retreat of the whole. The swarm’s defining danger
lies in its mass and persistence as a collective.
The Lantern Moth Swarm lairs in Ashreach. Its association with
fortified sites is therefore recorded as a matter of habit, not as
evidence that every manifestation originates within a fortress or

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
settlement. The designation siege-breaker describes its established
function against fortified positions.
The Lantern Moth Swarm was unleashed in The Leaden Accord. This event
remains the principal deployment record attached to the creature in the
present catalogue. The entry establishes use, not ownership, command,
or cause; no such attribution is entered here.
Field Recognition
- Dense cloud formation.
- Mothlike constituent forms.
- Eerie visual impression of lantern-light.
- Restless and overwhelming movement.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
- Escape considered difficult once the collective has closed around a
position.
- Serious threat to fortified positions.
Assessment
Concern Codex determination
Operational role Siege-breaker
Collective behavior Disruptive and overwhelming
Evasion Difficult
Threat rating 6
The Lantern Moth Swarm is consequently catalogued as a creature whose
danger derives from concentration, visual disruption, and pressure
against defensive works. Its individual moths do not define the
encounter. The swarm does.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Plate - Marsh Revenant: consult the plate for the recorded figures.
Marsh Revenant
Classification Record
Subject Marsh Revenant
Nature Revenant of stagnant, hostile ground
Habit siege-breaker
Lair Greyfell Citadel
Primary Function Shattering fortified resistance
Disposition Tireless, impersonal hostility
The Marsh Revenant is a siege-breaker, defined by its ability to
shatter fortified resistance. It is not a guardian of walls, nor a
creature properly contained by walls. Its presence turns defense into
desperation. Where resistance has been arranged behind stone, timber,
earthworks, or other fortification, the Marsh Revenant advances as a
direct negation of that preparation.
The Marsh Revenant is a revenant of stagnant, hostile ground. Marsh-wet
decay clings to its corpse-like figure, while its frame possesses the
grim solidity of a breaker of walls. Its appearance suggests both
burial and prolonged exposure to foul water: a body preserved without

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
mercy, hardened without purpose, and burdened by the weight of the
ground from which it arose. No ornament is required to identify it. Its
mass, condition, and forward motion are sufficient.
Its demeanor is one of tireless, impersonal hostility. The Marsh
Revenant does not threaten, negotiate, or display recognizable passion.
It advances with the inevitability of the dead. Delay does not diminish
its intent. Obstacles do not invite reconsideration. Its movement is
therefore treated as a pressure upon the entire defensive position
rather than as the approach of a single combatant.
Marsh Revenant - habit: siege-breaker
The Marsh Revenant lairs in Greyfell Citadel. The site is accordingly
recorded as a place of military concern, regardless of the condition of
its walls or the strength of its garrison. A defense confronted by the
creature must be understood as already compromised in principle. The
relevant question is not whether the structure can withstand an
ordinary assault, but how long its defenders can maintain organized
resistance while the Revenant advances.
For field identification, observers are instructed to distinguish the
creature’s corpse-like form from ordinary remains by its purposeful
motion and wall-breaking solidity. Stagnant decay alone is not
sufficient evidence. The determining signs are the convergence of
marsh-wet corruption, relentless advance, and the visible conversion of
defensive confidence into desperation.
The accompanying numbered plate records the Marsh Revenant’s figures.
Consult the plate for those measurements and other recorded values;

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
they are not reproduced in this entry. Its operational significance is
summarized here: the Marsh Revenant is encountered as a moving breach,
a manifestation of hostile ground, and a persistent assault upon the
idea that fortification guarantees safety.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Pale Stag of Omens
Classification Record
Name Pale Stag of Omens
Threat rating 5
Habit burrowing horror
Lair Hollowreach
Recorded event Unleashed in The Winter Reckoning
The Pale Stag of Omens is a burrowing horror of serious threat. Its
title is not ornamental. The designation identifies two concurrent
properties: its subterranean nature and the portentous impression
carried by its presence. It is therefore catalogued as both a physical
danger and an omen-bearing creature.
The Pale Stag of Omens appears as a pallid stag. Its antlered form is
unmistakable, yet the animal resemblance does not lessen its horror.
The antlers are the defining feature of its silhouette; the pallor of
its body gives the creature a corpse-like aspect without rendering it
inert or diminished. Observers consistently report that the form itself
carries an unmistakable sense of omen.
Its demeanor is quiet. It does not require spectacle to inspire dread.
The Pale Stag of Omens produces fear through quiet foreboding: the
apprehension that its appearance signifies what may follow. This effect
is considered intrinsic to the creature’s presence rather than
dependent upon a declared threat or visible act.
The known lair of the Pale Stag of Omens is Hollowreach. The location
is accordingly treated as a site of elevated concern. Any indication of
subterranean movement, disturbed ground, or a pallid antlered outline
within Hollowreach warrants classification as a possible manifestation
of the creature. Such indications do not establish the creature’s
presence by themselves.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Pale Stag of Omens was unleashed in The Winter Reckoning. This
event remains the principal recorded association attached to the
creature in the current codex. The record establishes its release, but
does not by itself define the full extent of the creature’s activity or
subsequent whereabouts.
Its threat rating: 5 places it among serious hazards requiring
disciplined assessment. The rating should not be interpreted as a
measure of its omen, symbolism, or psychological effect. It records the
creature’s standing as a danger; the dread produced by its quiet
foreboding is a separate characteristic.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Field annotation: Avoid treating the Pale Stag of Omens as a
conventional beast. Its stag-like appearance is certain, but its
classification as a burrowing horror is equally certain. The pallid
body, antlered form, subterranean habit, and portentous presence must
be considered together.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Salt-Blind Leviathan
The Salt-Blind Leviathan is a creature classified as a siege-breaker of
moderate threat. Its defining characteristics are immense destructive
force and an inability to rely on sight. It does not present the aspect
of a swift hunter or a calculating stalker. Its movement conveys
ponderous, relentless pressure: a continuous advance that treats
resistance as a condition to be endured rather than a barrier to be
avoided.
Classification Record
Name Salt-Blind Leviathan
Type Creature
Threat rating 4
Habit siege-breaker
Lair Greythrone
The Salt-Blind Leviathan appears as a vast leviathan, its body marked
by pale, salt-crusted features. Sightless eyes occupy the expected
place upon its head, but provide no reliable faculty of perception. The
creature is therefore defined not merely by blindness, but by the
absence of sight as a meaningful dependence. Its conduct must be
understood through pressure, disturbance, and the persistence of its
advance rather than through visible attention or directed observation.
Its destructive force is immense. This force is expressed most
characteristically against fortified resistance, where the creature’s
mass and inexorable motion become instruments of breach. The
designation siege-breaker describes its established habit, not a
specialized weapon or a temporary condition. It is suited to the
reduction of barriers by sustained impact and pressure. No account
should treat its lack of sight as evidence of weakness. The Salt-Blind
Leviathan remains dangerous precisely because its progress does not

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
require ordinary visual certainty.
The creature’s demeanor is ponderous and relentless. It does not convey
panic, haste, or deliberation in familiar proportions. Instead, it
imposes the impression of a burden moving under its own inevitable
weight. Witnesses may perceive the approach as slow, but slowness must
not be confused with hesitation. The creature’s pressure is the
relevant measure: constant, difficult to redirect, and destructive when
allowed to continue.
Salt-Blind Leviathan lairs in Greythrone. The lair designation
establishes its recorded place of habitation and should be treated as
the primary reference for assessments concerning its presence. Where
the creature is identified, its inability to rely on sight and its

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
immense destructive force are both operational concerns. Containment
estimates must account for the creature’s vast scale, pale salt-crusted
exterior, sightless eyes, and relentless siege-breaking habit.
Assessment: Salt-Blind Leviathan — threat rating: 4.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Plate - The Cinder-Wrought Aegis: consult the plate for the recorded
figures.
The Cinder-Wrought Aegis
Classification: Artifact Artifact class: regalia Forging site:
Embermarch Current housing: Gloamreach Forged: 342 AS
The Cinder-Wrought Aegis is regalia shaped by the legacy of the
Sundering. Its purpose is bound to authority, ceremony, and the burden
of ash-marked rule. It is not catalogued as a weapon, implement, or
vessel. Its significance lies in the office it represents and in the
formal weight imposed upon those who would preserve, display, or invoke
it.
The Aegis appears as imposing regalia worked in a cinder-dark style.
Its surfaces suggest fire-scarred craftsmanship: severe planes,
darkened finishes, and workmanship that presents damage as part of its
intended dignity. No softness is attributed to its appearance. Its
visual language is one of endurance beneath ruin.
Its demeanor carries an austere atmosphere of sovereignty endured
beneath ruin. This quality is not described as ornament, illusion, or
enchantment in the surviving register. It is a recognized impression
produced by the artifact’s form, condition, and ceremonial purpose. The

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Aegis therefore belongs among relics whose authority is communicated
through presence rather than ornament alone.
The Cinder-Wrought Aegis was forged at Embermarch. It is housed in
Gloamreach. These locations are retained as separate entries in the
armory record and are not to be conflated. The place of forging
establishes its origin; the place of housing establishes its recorded
custody.
The Cinder-Wrought Aegis's forged is 342 AS. Popular accounts wrongly
claim otherwise. This correction is authoritative. Scribes are to
preserve the date as 342 AS in inventories, ceremonial rolls, and
citations concerning the artifact.
Register Record
Name The Cinder-Wrought Aegis
Class Regalia
Origin Forged at Embermarch
Housing Housed in Gloamreach
Forged 342 AS
The accompanying numbered plate records the artifact’s figures and
provides the proper visual reference for its documented proportions and
features. Consult the plate when those recorded figures are required;
the plate, rather than an unauthorised summary, is the controlling
reference for that purpose.
In ceremonial contexts, the Aegis should be treated as a burden-bearing
emblem of ash-marked rule. Its cinder-dark presentation does not lessen
its authority. It defines that authority as something maintained
beneath ruin, under the discipline of ceremony, and without any promise
of comfort.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Crown of Burned Names
Artifact class: ward Forged: 266 AS Attunement cost: 60 Forge-site:
Hollowvale Current housing: Blackford
Classification
The Crown of Burned Names is a ward whose defining character lies in
the tension between protection and the erasure carried by burned names.
Its classification establishes its function as a protective artifact,
but does not lessen the memorial quality imposed by its form or title.
The Crown of Burned Names was forged at Hollowvale in 266 AS. It is
housed in Blackford. These locations are entered as separate points of
record: Hollowvale is the forge-site, while Blackford is the present
housing site.
Attunement cost is 60. The cost reflects the burden of establishing a
guarded identity in the presence of names that have been burned away.
No lesser designation is recognized for partial attunement.
Appearance
The Crown of Burned Names is a crown of blackened, name-scarred
material. Its silhouette is stark and funerary. The surface bears the
visible consequence of burned names rather than a polished declaration
of rank. The object should therefore be read first as a ward of
remembrance and guarded identity, and only second as a crown.
The material is described by its blackening and scars. The scars are
integral to its identification. Removal, concealment, or alteration of
those marks would compromise the artifact’s recognizable presentation,
though the dossier assigns no separate mechanism to such treatment.
Demeanor
The Crown of Burned Names imposes a hushed atmosphere of remembrance,

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
loss, and guarded identity. This atmosphere is a persistent aspect of
the artifact’s demeanor. It is neither celebratory nor openly martial.
Its presence favors restraint, silence, and the careful preservation of
what remains identifiable.
The ward’s protective identity is therefore inseparable from erasure.
The burned name is not merely absent; it is carried as a mark. The
crown offers no simple distinction between defense and mourning. Its
authority derives from that unresolved condition.
Registry Note
Register field Recorded entry
Name The Crown of Burned Names
Artifact class ward

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Forged 266 AS
Forged at Hollowvale
Attunement cost 60
Housed in Blackford
The Crown of Burned Names is to be catalogued under ward, with its
funerary silhouette and name-scarred material retained as primary
identifiers. Its recorded history begins with its forging at Hollowvale
in 266 AS and continues through its housing in Blackford.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Hollow Edge
Artifact Class: ward Forged: 216 AS Forged at: Hollowvale Housed in:
Crookgate Keep Attunement Cost: 21
Catalogue Field Recorded Determination
Name The Hollow Edge
Artifact class ward
Year of forging 216 AS
Place of forging Hollowvale
Current housing Crookgate Keep
Attunement cost 21
Visual identity A ward bearing the name The Hollow Edge
Demeanor Emptiness and severity
Classification
The Hollow Edge is a ward forged in 216 AS. Its classification is fixed
as ward. The record assigns no alternate class, derivative designation,
or subordinate form. In catalogues, the article is entered under its
full name: The Hollow Edge.
Its visual identity is that of a ward bearing the name The Hollow Edge.
This distinction is descriptive rather than interpretive. The
appearance establishes recognition in inventories and examination
chambers; it does not, by itself, establish the extent or nature of the
ward’s operation.
Provenance
The Hollow Edge was forged at Hollowvale in 216 AS. This place and year
constitute its recorded forging provenance. The dating is expressed in
the calendar of the Ashen Era and is not to be converted into an
alternate reckoning.
The artifact is housed in Crookgate Keep. Housing is the recorded
custodial condition of The Hollow Edge. It should not be confused with
the place of forging: Hollowvale is recorded as the site at which the
ward was forged, while Crookgate Keep is recorded as the site in which
it is housed.
Attunement
Attunement to The Hollow Edge costs 21. The value is entered without

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
supplementary measure. Any claimant, bearer, or examiner consulting the
armory register must account for this cost before attempting
attunement.
Demeanor

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
table: A ward bearing the name The Hollow Edge

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Hollow Edge suggests an atmosphere of emptiness and severity. This
demeanor is consistently associated with its catalogued presence. It is
not described as warmth, abundance, or ease. The impression remains
austere: an absence made perceptible, bounded by the strict visual
identity of a ward.
The Hollow Edge is therefore indexed by four controlling particulars:
its class as a ward, its forging at Hollowvale in 216 AS, its
attunement cost of 21, and its housing in Crookgate Keep. These
particulars define the artifact’s established entry in Codex Vaeloria
II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Psalter of Seven Sorrows
Artifact Record
The Psalter of Seven Sorrows is a ward forged in 119 AS. Its artifact
class is ward. The recorded place of forging is Ironfell Citadel, and
the forging occurred in 119 AS. The artifact is housed in Fenthrone.
Attunement to The Psalter of Seven Sorrows costs 49. No alternate cost,
classification, or forging record is entered in this volume.
Registry Field Recorded Entry
Name The Psalter of Seven Sorrows
Artifact class ward
Forged 119 AS
Forged at Ironfell Citadel
Housed in Fenthrone
Attunement cost 49
Appearance
The Psalter of Seven Sorrows presents the visual identity of a ward
bearing the name The Psalter of Seven Sorrows. Its designation is not
supplementary to its appearance; the named identity is part of the
artifact’s recorded presentation. Examination is therefore to
distinguish the ward as catalogued, without assigning an unrecorded
shape, material, ornament, or mechanism.
Demeanor
The Psalter of Seven Sorrows carries an atmosphere of sorrow shaped by
its name. This quality is catalogued as demeanor rather than as a
measured effect. The record establishes the presence of sorrow in the
artifact’s character, but does not assign a separate manifestation,
duration, target, or range.
The term “Psalter” is retained as part of the artifact’s exact name. It
does not alter the artifact class. The Psalter of Seven Sorrows remains
a ward, and its attunement cost remains 49.
Custody and Provenance
The registered provenance is concise: The Psalter of Seven Sorrows was

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
forged at Ironfell Citadel in 119 AS and is housed in Fenthrone. These
entries are distinct. Ironfell Citadel is recorded as the place of
forging; Fenthrone is recorded as the place of housing.
No further transfer, bearer, keeper, construction method, material, or
operative capacity is entered under this artifact. Such matters are
outside the surviving record and are not to be supplied by inference.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Catalog determination: The Psalter of Seven Sorrows is a ward of
sorrowful demeanor, forged at Ironfell Citadel in 119 AS, housed in
Fenthrone, and requiring an attunement cost of 49.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Sceptre of Final Winter
Artifact Class: ward Forged: 87 AS Forge-Site: Emberdeep Current
Housing: Palewell Abbey Attunement Cost: 55
The Sceptre of Final Winter is a ward forged at Emberdeep in 87 AS. Its
present housing is Palewell Abbey. These particulars constitute the
accepted registry record; no alternate forge-site or housing is
recognized in the relevant entries.
Registry Measure Record
Name The Sceptre of Final Winter
Classification ward
Forging 87 AS
Place of Forging Emberdeep
Housing Palewell Abbey
Attunement Cost 55
The object’s visual identity is that of a ward bearing the name The
Sceptre of Final Winter. Its form is therefore to be read as an
instrument of designation as much as an implement of use. The name is
not ornamental in the catalogue sense: it is the identifying mark by
which the artifact is distinguished from other wards.
Its demeanor is equally explicit. The Sceptre of Final Winter radiates
an atmosphere of cold finality. This quality is perceptible without
requiring any additional interpretation of the ward’s construction. It
is the principal environmental impression associated with the artifact
and remains the standard description used in formal inventories.
Attunement to The Sceptre of Final Winter costs 55. The cost is
recorded as a fixed requirement of the artifact and is not to be
conflated with its classification as a ward. No additional attunement
conditions are entered in this volume.
The forging record is likewise fixed: The Sceptre of Final Winter -
forged: 87 AS. The associated place is Emberdeep, giving the complete

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
entry as follows: The Sceptre of Final Winter forged at Emberdeep (in
87 AS). The housing record is separate and current in function: The
Sceptre of Final Winter housed in Palewell Abbey.
For catalogue purposes, the artifact should be cited under its full
name. Abbreviated references may obscure its identity and are
unsuitable for transfer records, attunement ledgers, or ward
inventories. The accepted designation remains The Sceptre of Final
Winter, with artifact class ward, forging year 87 AS, attunement cost
55, forge-site Emberdeep, and housing Palewell Abbey.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
The Silent Psalter
Classification Record
Name The Silent Psalter
Artifact class instrument
Forged 204 AS
Forged at Fenspire
Attunement cost 49
Housed in Marrowwatch
The Silent Psalter is an instrument forged in 204 AS, at Fenspire. Its
present housing is Marrowwatch. These particulars are sufficient for
formal identification; no supplementary title or alternate designation
is recognized in the catalogue.
Though made for expression, The Silent Psalter is defined by silence.
Its construction provides no ordinary promise of song, proclamation, or
release. Instead, the artifact imposes a grave discipline upon any
wielder who seeks to establish attunement. The required attunement cost
is 49. This cost is not treated as incidental notation. It is the
principal measure by which the Psalter’s burden is assessed.
The artifact resembles a somber devotional instrument. Its form is
muted and visibly fashioned for silent use. Surfaces, fittings, and
resonant elements present no theatrical ornamentation. The whole is
arranged toward restraint rather than display. Whether held, prepared,
or set aside, The Silent Psalter maintains the visual character of a
thing intended to contain expression rather than produce it.
Its demeanor evokes restrained sorrow and an oppressive quiet that
resists release. This quality is persistent. The Psalter does not
merely lack sound; it conveys the pressure of sound withheld. Observers
commonly describe its presence in terms of diminished breath, closed
recitation, and discipline maintained beyond comfort. Such descriptions

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
are classificatory impressions, not evidence of an audible effect.
Attribute Codex determination
Intended principle Expression under silence
Governing condition Grave discipline
Emotional impression Restrained sorrow
Environmental impression Oppressive quiet
Release Resisted
The Silent Psalter is therefore not to be evaluated as a conventional
instrument. Its significance lies in the contradiction preserved by its
making: it was made for expression, yet its defining character is

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
silence. The artifact’s use requires the wielder to accept that
contradiction rather than resolve it through performance.
Attunement records must preserve the stated cost of 49 without
abbreviation or substitution. Housing records must identify
Marrowwatch. Forge records must identify Fenspire and the year 204 AS.
Any entry omitting these locations or the year is incomplete.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Plate - The Thrice-Bound Edge: consult the plate for the recorded
figures.
The Thrice-Bound Edge
Artifact Class: Regalia Forged: 123 AS Forged at: Hollowreach Housed
in: Crookvale Attunement Cost: None recorded
The Thrice-Bound Edge is regalia forged in 123 AS. Its defining record
is concise: the artifact is identified by its name, its class, its
place of forging, and its current housing. No attunement cost is
recorded for it. The absence of such a cost is a condition of the
record, not an indication of function, accessibility, or permitted use.
The Thrice-Bound Edge was forged at Hollowreach in 123 AS. It is housed
in Crookvale. These locations are preserved as separate entries in the
artifact register and are not to be conflated. The register supplies no
further qualification concerning transfer, custody, or intervening
possession.
Registry Field Recorded Entry
Name The Thrice-Bound Edge
Artifact class regalia
Forged 123 AS

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Forged at Hollowreach
Housed in Crookvale
Attunement cost No cost recorded
Its visual identity is that of regalia bearing the name The
Thrice-Bound Edge. The designation is therefore descriptive of its
recognized presentation, without establishing a material inventory,
construction method, or ceremonial office. No additional physical
specification is admitted into the defining record.
The artifact conveys a restrained, binding atmosphere. This impression
is catalogued as demeanor. It does not, by itself, establish a power,
requirement, restriction, oath, or consequence. Readers and custodians
are directed to distinguish the recorded atmosphere from any
interpretation attached to it.
The Thrice-Bound Edge is consequently classified by restraint in
description as much as by its formal category. It is regalia; it was
forged at Hollowreach in 123 AS; and it is housed in Crookvale. The
entry records no attunement cost and does not supplement that omission
with conjecture.
For the artifact’s recorded figures, consult the accompanying numbered
plate. The plate is authoritative for those figures; they are
intentionally not reproduced in this entry. Its annotations should be
read alongside the registry fields above, with the artifact’s exact
name retained in all citations: The Thrice-Bound Edge.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Plate - The Thrice-Bound Lantern: consult the plate for the recorded
figures.
The Thrice-Bound Lantern
Classification Record
Artifact The Thrice-Bound Lantern
Artifact class ward
Forged 72 AS
Forged at Stormmarch
Housed in Hollowvale
The Thrice-Bound Lantern is a ward whose function is protective rather
than destructive. Its strength lies in restraint and containment. It is
not recorded as a device for pursuit, assault, or revelation. Its
construction expresses a single governing principle: danger must be
held, limited, and denied passage.
The ward was forged at Stormmarch in 72 AS. The circumstances of its
forging are not material to its classification. Its established origin
remains Stormmarch, and its forged date remains 72 AS. The Thrice-Bound
Lantern is housed in Hollowvale.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Its exterior is immediately legible. The lantern bears three visible
bindings, each forming part of the object’s severe, warding silhouette.
These bindings are not ornamental distinctions. They constitute the
visible sign of its threefold binding and define the artifact’s
recognized identity. The casing presents no invitation to handling
beyond necessity. Its shape is deliberate, closed, and resistant to
casual interpretation.
The Thrice-Bound Lantern radiates guarded stillness. The effect is
comparable to a watch maintained without motion: perpetual, controlled,
and without display. It appears as though the ward is continually
holding danger at bay. This demeanor is consistent with its
classification as a ward and with the containment principle established
by its binding.
No claim should be made that the lantern destroys what it restrains.
The available record supports containment, not annihilation. Likewise,
its presence should not be treated as evidence that danger has been
removed. The ward’s purpose is better understood as the maintenance of
a boundary and the denial of breach.
The threefold binding is therefore both structural and doctrinal. It
identifies The Thrice-Bound Lantern as a protective object whose power
depends upon limitation. The artifact’s guarded stillness, severe form,
and restrained function are mutually confirming characteristics.
For the recorded figures associated with the artifact, consult the
numbered plate accompanying this entry. The plate preserves the
relevant measurements and other figures without replacing the

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
classifications given above. In field inventories, the artifact should
be entered under its exact name and artifact class: The Thrice-Bound
Lantern — ward.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Plate - Thorn Wraith: consult the plate for the recorded figures.
Thorn Wraith
Entry Recorded designation
Subject Thorn Wraith (creature)
Habit Thorn Wraith - habit: dream-feeder
Lair Thorn Wraith lairs in Ironfell Citadel
Manifestation Ghostly, thorn-threaded form
Temperament Intimate, predatory, patient
Nature
The Thorn Wraith is a dream-feeder, drawing its nature from the
invasion and consumption of dreams. It belongs as much to the terror of
sleep as to the waking world. Its presence is therefore not confined to
a chamber, a bed, or any place where the body rests. The creature’s
proper domain is the vulnerable interval in which thought loses its
ordinary defenses.
The Thorn Wraith does not present itself as a simple apparition. It is
a pressure upon the mind, an intrusion that may be felt before it is
perceived. Sleep becomes its opening. Dreams become its substance. The

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
table: Thorn Wraith lairs in Ironfell Citadel

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
distinction between a remembered fear and an encountered entity is
consequently unreliable in any account concerning it.
Appearance
The Thorn Wraith has a ghostly form threaded with thorn-like shapes,
giving its outline a cruel and insubstantial character. These shapes
define neither armor nor natural anatomy in any stable sense. They
appear instead as part of the creature’s manifestation: a barbed
contour surrounding an otherwise wavering presence.
Its outline may seem near at one instant and remote at the next. Such
impressions should not be treated as evidence of ordinary movement. The
form is bound to the conditions of perception under which it is
observed, particularly when the observer is exhausted, sleeping, or
emerging from sleep.
Demeanor
The Thorn Wraith feels intimate and predatory, haunting the mind with
the patience of hunger. It is not characterized by haste. Its conduct
is one of sustained proximity, allowing apprehension to deepen before
the intrusion becomes unmistakable.
Reports concerning the creature should distinguish physical observation
from dream experience wherever possible. This distinction may remain
unresolved; the Thorn Wraith’s nature expressly occupies both
conditions. Fear alone does not establish its presence, but recurring
signs of invasion should not be dismissed as ordinary dreaming.
Lair
Thorn Wraith lairs in Ironfell Citadel. The lair designation identifies
its established place of habitation, not the limit of its influence.
Encounters beyond the lair may involve the creature’s dream-feeding

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
nature rather than a conventional departure from its haunt.
For the recorded figures associated with this entry, consult the
accompanying numbered plate.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Vault Chitin
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Classification Record
Subject Vault Chitin
Nature Creature
Threat rating 5
Habit Dream-feeder
Lair Greyfell Citadel
Recorded deployment The War of Endless Vigil
Summary
Vault Chitin is a dream-feeder of serious threat. It is associated with
sealed, enclosed places and feeds upon dreams. Its presence is
therefore most consistent with locations in which access, escape, and
ordinary perception are restricted. The creature is not defined by open
pursuit alone; its principal danger concerns the integrity of the
sleeping mind.
Vault Chitin lairs in Greyfell Citadel. The site’s sealed character is
consistent with the creature’s known associations, though the record
does not establish whether the lair preceded or followed its
occupation. Vault Chitin was unleashed in The War of Endless Vigil.
This entry records that deployment without assigning motive, command,
or duration beyond the stated fact.
Appearance
Vault Chitin presents a hard, chitinous form suggestive of something
emerging from a vault. Its body conveys enclosure made animate: rigid
surfaces, guarded recesses, and the visual impression of pressure
forcing its way through a sealed boundary. The exact arrangement of its
limbs, sensory organs, and openings is not fixed in the surviving
description. No ornamental interpretation is required. Its recognizable
traits are hardness, chitinous construction, and the suggestion of
emergence from a vault.
Mental Effect
Vault Chitin feels invasive, alien, and oppressive within the mind.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
This effect is not merely an observer’s discomfort. The creature’s
association with dreams places the sleeping state within its sphere of
threat. Reports concerning its presence should therefore distinguish
between physical manifestation and intrusion perceived during sleep.
Confusion between these conditions is considered a normal consequence
of contact.

chunks.doc_title: Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
Codex Vaeloria II: Armory of Relics and Bestiary
chunks.text:
Dreams encountered in proximity to Vault Chitin are not to be treated
as reliable testimony. They may reflect the creature’s feeding habit,
its oppressive mental presence, or ordinary uncertainty; the record
does not provide a method for separating these causes. Wakefulness is
likewise not sufficient evidence that the creature has withdrawn.
Threat Assessment
Risk Assessment
Physical presence Serious threat
Dream exposure Serious threat
Enclosed locations Elevated concern
Mental pressure Invasive, alien, oppressive
Vault Chitin is to be classified according to the recorded threat
rating: 5. Its habit is recorded exactly as dream-feeder. Reports
naming Vault Chitin should preserve the distinction between confirmed
location, recorded deployment, and inferred behavior.

Faction Classification: noble house Seat: Ironfell Citadel Doctrine: Ancient noble dynasty claiming descent from the last Sunder-Kings.
House Morvain is an ancient noble house whose authority rests upon a dynastic claim and the weight of its antiquity. It claims descent from the last Sunder-Kings, a lineage asserted as the foundation of its legitimacy. This claim is not presented as a secondary ornament to its rule; it is the central doctrine by which the house defines its station and expects recognition.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The house is seated at Ironfell Citadel. Its seat, identity, and conduct conform to an aristocratic and kingly presentation shaped by its claimed descent from the Sunder-Kings. Ceremonial display, heraldic emphasis, and formal address are treated as instruments of continuity rather than mere decoration. The house’s antiquity is itself a political resource.
House Morvain carries itself with ancestral pride and a guarded sense of entitlement. Its representatives are characterized by restraint, formal reserve, and an expectation that precedence should be acknowledged. Such conduct reflects the house’s view of itself as an enduring dynasty rather than a temporary claimant among the powers of the Ashen Era.
The record identifies House Morvain as belligerent in The War of Endless Vigil. The record also identifies House Morvain as belligerent in The Purge of Blackport. These entries establish the house’s participation as a belligerent in both conflicts; they do not, in this entry, define the full causes, operations, or outcomes of either.
House Morvain’s standing therefore derives from three mutually reinforcing assertions: noble status, descent from the last Sunder-Kings, and the accumulated authority of antiquity. Its posture remains kingly in appearance, dynastic in doctrine, and guarded in demeanor. The house’s claim is the basis upon which it presents its right to regard itself as a principal power.

chunks.text:
Classification: Conflict Beginning: 297 AS Ending: 301 AS Victor: The Ashen Vanguard Recorded outcome: Collapsed into a decade of guerrilla reprisals
The Accord of Mournthrone began in 297 AS and ended in 301 AS with The Ashen Vanguard named victor. The title is retained in the annals despite the accord’s failure to produce a durable settlement. Its visual identity is that of a broken accord overshadowed by Mournthrone and The Ashen Vanguard. Its demeanor is less that of a settled victory than a sullen prelude to reprisal.
The principal recorded actions are as follows:

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
table: The Accord of Mournthrone waged at Crookvale.
The Accord of Mournthrone devastated Fenspire.
The Accord of Mournthrone devastated Hollowvale.
The Accord of Mournthrone waged at Vharencrag Fortress.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
These entries do not describe a continuous advance or a conclusive pacification. They establish the geographic record of the conflict and the visible damage associated with its progress. The devastation of Fenspire and Hollowvale remains attached to the conflict’s formal chronology; the actions at Crookvale and Vharencrag Fortress remain attached to its military record.
The declared result was victory for The Ashen Vanguard. The actual result was less stable. The Accord of Mournthrone collapsed into a decade of guerrilla reprisals, preserving the conflict in dispersed violence after its formal ending. Accordingly, the designation of victor does not constitute proof of complete control, reconciliation, or lasting submission.
The concealed record gives the conflict a second interpretation. The secret truth is that the losing commander was bribed to withdraw. This fact alters the apparent meaning of the final result without removing The Ashen Vanguard’s status as victor. The withdrawal is therefore catalogued as a concealed cause of collapse rather than as a separate engagement.
The numbered plate accompanying this entry preserves the recorded figures. Consult the plate for those figures; they are not reproduced here. For purposes of the annals, the essential determination remains unchanged: The Accord of Mournthrone began in 297 AS, ended in 301 AS, named The Ashen Vanguard victor, and left a decade of guerrilla reprisals in its wake.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text: The Ashen Vanguard is a knightly order sworn to contain the Ley-ruins left by the Sundering. Its doctrine is not custodial in the passive sense. It defines containment as an active military obligation, requiring militant discipline, controlled force, and uninterrupted vigilance wherever dangerous remnants persist.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Ashen Vanguard is seated at Vharenford. This seat is the principal point from which its order is identified in surviving registers. No distinction is made in those registers between its administrative authority and its military purpose: both are subordinated to the containment of the Ley-ruins.
Its visual identity is that of a militant, knightly order marked by the grim legacy of the Ley-ruins. Equipment, bearing, and ceremony are consequently treated as instruments of warning as much as instruments of war. The order presents no softened interpretation of its charge. Its appearance communicates the hazards it confronts and the severity with which it addresses them.
The Vanguard’s demeanor is severe, disciplined, and constantly watchful. Individual conduct is expected to reflect the order’s collective doctrine. Uncertainty, negligence, and uncontrolled contact with dangerous remnants are incompatible with its stated purpose. The order therefore maintains a posture of readiness even when no engagement is recorded.
The Ashen Vanguard was belligerent in The War of Drowned Light. It was also belligerent in The Accord of Mournthrone, where The Ashen Vanguard is recorded as victor. The order was further belligerent in The Leaden Accord. These entries establish its recurring presence in the military record without altering its primary classification as a knightly order.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text: In all formal descriptions, the central fact remains unchanged: The Ashen Vanguard is a militant order sworn to contain the Ley-ruins left by the Sundering. Its authority derives from that oath, its appearance bears the mark of that duty, and its conduct is governed by the discipline required to enforce it. Vharenford remains the seat by which the order is located in the annals.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Bleeding Crown is a royalist remnant fighting to restore the shattered monarchy. Its cause is defined by loyalty to the monarchy and opposition to the realm’s fractured condition. It does not recognize the shattered condition of the realm as a legitimate settlement. Its stated purpose is restoration rather than accommodation.
The Bleeding Crown is seated at Blackford. This seat constitutes its established center of authority and the principal location from which its royalist claim is maintained.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
table: Royalist remnant fighting to restore the shattered monarchy.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The faction’s loyalty is directed toward the monarchy as an institution, not toward the realm’s present divisions. Its opposition to the fractured condition of the realm informs its rhetoric, recruitment, and conduct. In practice, the distinction between restoration and reprisal is frequently narrow.
The Bleeding Crown is fervent in declaration and embittered by the monarchy’s shattering. It is determined in pursuit of restoration. These qualities are not ornamental descriptions; they are recognized characteristics of the faction’s public bearing and internal discipline.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text: Its visual identity is royalist and wounded, evoking a crown that has endured the shattering of the monarchy. Crown forms, damaged regalia, and marks of fracture are consistent with this presentation. The symbolism presents survival as proof of rightful endurance. It does not depict an unbroken crown. The wound is retained as evidence, warning, and claim.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Bleeding Crown was a belligerent in The War of Endless Vigil and is recorded as its victor. The record establishes both its participation and its victory; it does not diminish the faction’s character as a remnant. Its success in that war is used by the faction as confirmation that the royalist cause remains capable of prevailing.
The Bleeding Crown was also a belligerent in The Accord of Mournthrone. This designation records its presence as a party to that accord’s belligerent order. No broader conclusion is entered here regarding the accord’s settlement or subsequent force.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text: The Bleeding Crown remains defined by restoration, monarchy, and resistance to fragmentation. Its authority is royalist in origin, wounded in appearance, and fervent, embittered, and determined in demeanor. Codex classification: royalist remnant.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Iron-Ring Cartel is a merchant cartel seated at Hollowreach. Its doctrine is recorded as follows:
> The Iron-Ring Cartel — doctrine: Mercantile league running contraband through the ruined trade roads.
The Cartel is a mercantile league organized around commerce conducted across the remnants of the realm’s trade routes. Its operations concern the movement, exchange, and concealment of contraband through roads damaged or abandoned after the Sundering. The organization’s structure is consequently commercial rather than feudal, with authority expressed through control of trade, access, and passage.
Its visual identity is mercantile and hard-edged. Iron, sealed cargo, marked ledgers, guarded wagons, and reinforced trade gear are consistent with its cartel structure and contraband trade. These signs are not ornamental. They indicate a faction whose public identity is inseparable from the practical demands of commerce conducted beyond lawful channels.
The Cartel’s demeanor is calculating and practical. It is comfortable operating beyond lawful trade and does not present illegality as a moral distinction requiring explanation. Decisions are assessed by utility, risk, access, and return. Negotiation is therefore treated as an instrument of commerce rather than a display of trust.

The Iron-Ring Cartel belligerent in The Leaden Accord; The Iron-Ring Cartel victor of The Leaden Accord

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
These records establish the Cartel as a recurring participant in the armed and political contests of the Ashen Era. They do not alter its primary classification. The Iron-Ring Cartel remains a merchant cartel, and its stated doctrine remains the operation of a mercantile league running contraband through the ruined trade roads.
At Hollowreach, its seated authority is understood through this same commercial logic. The Cartel’s presence is defined by transaction, movement, and controlled access. Its hard-edged appearance and calculating demeanor are functional expressions of its organization, not separate traditions. The faction’s conduct beyond lawful trade is therefore consistent with its doctrine, its structure, and its established record as belligerent and victor.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
Classification: Conflict Beginning: 330 AS End: 342 AS Recorded casualty figure: 14011 Named victor: The Iron-Ring Cartel
The Leaden Accord was a prolonged military contest whose surviving record is defined less by conquest than by erasure. Its duration began in 330 AS and ended in 342 AS. The accepted outcome names The Iron-Ring Cartel as victor. This designation remains official despite the final destruction suffered by both opposing hosts.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Leaden Accord ended when both hosts were destroyed by a Ley-storm. The event rendered the declaration of victory administratively useful but militarily hollow. The recorded casualty figure is 14011. No surviving account establishes the final disposition of every combatant, and the visible remains support only the conclusion that mutual ruin followed the last engagement.
The principal contradiction lies in the artifact associated with the conflict. Public accounts state that it was destroyed. The hidden truth is that a supposedly destroyed artifact was in fact spirited away. Its absence is therefore treated as evidence of concealment rather than confirmation of destruction. The identity and present custody of the artifact are not established in this entry.
The Leaden Accord’s visual identity is leaden, storm-riven, and haunted by the absence of a supposedly destroyed artifact. Surviving depictions favor dim metal, fractured skies, vacant reliquaries, and structures reduced to inert silhouettes. These conventions do not signify a single battlefield; they signify the conflict’s condition of incomplete closure.
Its demeanor is the bleak stillness of mutual ruin concealed beneath a declared victory. This distinction is preserved in formal annotations: victory belongs to The Iron-Ring Cartel, while the hosts themselves were destroyed by a Ley-storm. The declaration and the destruction are both canonical, but they do not describe the same kind of success.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text: The devastation of Greyfell Citadel in 337 AS, Palewell Abbey in 338 AS, and Cindermere Hold in 338 AS marks the conflict’s destructive record. The engagement at Vharencrag Fortress in 341 AS stands as its last specifically recorded site before the ending in 342 AS.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
Classification: Conflict Period: 311 AS–321 AS Victor: The Iron-Ring Cartel Casualties: 70907 Outcome: Ended with the total rout of the aggressors
The Purge of Blackport began in 311 AS and ended in 321 AS. It caused 70907 casualties and ended with the total rout of the aggressors. The Iron-Ring Cartel emerged as victor.
The conflict’s recorded scope includes two designated theatres of devastation:

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
table: The Purge of Blackport waged at Fenspire (in 319 AS)
The Purge of Blackport devastated Gloamreach (in 320 AS)

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The official settlement attributes victory to The Iron-Ring Cartel and treats the rout of the aggressors as the conclusive military result. The record is therefore commonly cited as a model of merciless triumph: decisive, comprehensive, and without mitigation.
A concealed truth alters that judgment. The victors poisoned the wells of their own allies. This act is not presented as a secondary accident or an incidental contamination. It is the hidden instrument by which the apparent triumph must be understood. The same force that secured victory imposed ruin upon those aligned with it.
The Purge of Blackport has consequently retained two simultaneous classifications in the annals. Publicly, it is a victorious campaign ending in the total rout of the aggressors. In restricted accounts, it is a calculated betrayal concealed beneath the language of victory. The distinction is material: the casualty figure records the scale of the conflict, but does not by itself disclose the method used by the victors.
Appearance: Blackport under purge, marked by The Iron-Ring Cartel and poisoned water.
Demeanor: Merciless triumph soured by calculated betrayal.
The conflict’s enduring emblem is thus not the routed aggressor, nor the Cartel’s undisputed victory alone, but poisoned water within a victorious domain. Its records remain serviceable for determining dates, theatres, casualties, and outcome. They are less reliable when used to describe the moral character of the victory.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Silent Choir is a secretive priesthood whose religious authority is exercised through control of the historical record. Its doctrine assigns record, correction, suppression, and revision to a single sacred function. History is therefore not treated as a fixed inheritance. It is maintained as an instrument of order, subject to examination and alteration by the Choir.
The Silent Choir records history. It censors history. It rewrites history. These duties are not separate offices in the known account of the faction, but expressions of one doctrine. The Choir’s authority rests upon possession of the accepted version of events and upon the restriction of competing versions.
The Silent Choir is seated at Vharencrag Fortress. Its seat is associated with restrained religious practice, controlled access, and the keeping of records. The visual identity of The Silent Choir is priestly, restrained, and defined by secrecy and the keeping of records. Its appearance communicates neither pageantry nor open force. It presents the discipline of custody.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Choir is quiet, inscrutable, and deliberate in its handling of truth. Statements are measured. Omissions are consequential. Disclosure is treated as an act requiring the same care as inscription. The faction’s silence is therefore not an absence of policy; it is a method of policy.
Its custodians maintain a severe distinction between what may be preserved, what may be concealed, and what may be rewritten. The distinction is administered through religious authority rather than public consent. For this reason, the Choir’s records possess both archival and doctrinal weight.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Silent Choir was belligerent in The War of Drowned Light and was victor of The War of Drowned Light. The Silent Choir was belligerent in The War of Endless Vigil. The Silent Choir was belligerent in The Winter Reckoning.
No general account of these belligerencies is entered here beyond the stated record. The Choir’s own handling of the historical record remains a material consideration in all surviving accounts. Its victory in The War of Drowned Light is therefore recorded as an established factional result, while the form and interpretation of that result remain subject to the Choir’s doctrine.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
Classification: Conflict Period: 225 AS–235 AS Casualties: 64617 Recorded victor: The Silent Choir Outcome: Collapsed into a decade of guerrilla reprisals
The War of Drowned Light began in 225 AS and ended in 235 AS. Its duration is recorded without qualification, though the violence associated with it did not resolve into a clean termination. The War of Drowned Light collapsed into a decade of guerrilla reprisals, and its conclusion therefore signifies the end of the principal war rather than the restoration of settled order.
The conflict’s recorded casualty figure is 64617. This figure is preserved in the annals as the accepted total for the war. The surviving record does not treat the number as evidence of a decisive engagement or a single catastrophic event. Instead, it belongs to a campaign remembered for attrition, concealed operations, reprisals, and the persistence of violence after formal hostilities had ended.
