chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The War of Drowned Light victor was The Silent Choir. This designation remains the formal outcome in the principal annalistic tradition. A separate concealed record states that the spark that started it was staged by The Silent Choir. The victory and the secret staging are therefore entered together, though the latter was not presented as public cause during the conflict.
Its visual identity is one of drowned radiance, broken banners, and a war remembered through reprisals rather than triumph. Records concerning its battlefields frequently emphasize obscured light, damaged standards, and the absence of ceremonial closure. These features are classificatory rather than decorative: they distinguish the conflict from wars whose memory is organized around conquest or formal settlement.
Its demeanor is marked by concealed treachery, attrition, and unresolved vengeance. The designation applies both to the war itself and to its aftermath. The decade of guerrilla reprisals remains the principal reason the conflict is not treated as concluded in the conventional sense of victory, surrender, or reconciliation.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
Classification: Conflict Period: 247 AS–251 AS Recorded victor: The Bleeding Crown Casualty figure: 81577
The War of Endless Vigil began in 247 AS and ended in 251 AS. Its recorded conclusion was the total rout of the aggressors. The Bleeding Crown is recorded as the victor.
The conflict imposed severe destruction across the contested territories. The War of Endless Vigil devastated Crookvale in 249 AS. It devastated Thorncairn in 250 AS. The War of Endless Vigil was waged at Hollowreach in 251 AS.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
table: Ended with the total rout of the aggressors
The losing commander was bribed to withdraw

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The war’s visual identity is one of blood-marked watchfulness, exhausted armies, and an enemy line breaking under prolonged vigilance. Its imagery is therefore defined less by sudden triumph than by the persistence of forces that remain at their stations until opposition fails.
The conflict feels brutal and decisive on the surface. Its recorded outcome supports that appearance: the aggressors were totally routed, and The Bleeding Crown received the formal victory. This conclusion is not, however, a complete account of the war’s conduct.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The secret truth of the War of Endless Vigil is that the losing commander was bribed to withdraw. The withdrawal remains the concealed determinant behind the apparent final collapse. Accordingly, the war is classified as both a decisive rout and a corrupted victory.
This distinction is preserved in the annals without altering the official result. The Bleeding Crown remains the recorded victor. The total rout of the aggressors remains the recorded outcome. The hidden payment does not nullify either entry; it qualifies the means by which the conclusion was reached.
The casualty figure is recorded as 81577. The devastation of Crookvale, the devastation of Thorncairn, and the fighting at Hollowreach establish the war’s material imprint across its listed sites. Together with the concealed bribery, these records define the conflict as an episode of prolonged vigilance, exhaustion, betrayal, and final collapse.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
Classification: Conflict Period: 270 AS–283 AS Victor: The Iron-Ring Cartel Casualty figure: 27987
The Winter Reckoning began in 270 AS and ended in 283 AS. Its duration is recorded without interruption in the surviving annals, though the record of its final settlement remains materially incomplete. The conflict left 27987 casualties and concluded with The Iron-Ring Cartel identified as victor.
Its outcome was decided by a betrayal at the eleventh hour. This determination is accepted by the principal accounts, despite their disagreement concerning the identity and scope of the treachery. The concealed truth is that the victors poisoned the wells of their own allies. This fact is preserved in restricted testimony and is not treated as a battlefield rumor.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
table: The Winter Reckoning waged at Stormmarch (in 276 AS)

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The documented sites indicate a conflict marked by movement through exposed winter ground, fortified holdings, and contested sources of water. No single surviving account establishes the full sequence of engagements. The destruction of Cindermere Hold and Marrowwell Abbey is nevertheless entered as a direct consequence of the conflict’s passage.
Its visual identity is one of winter, betrayal, and the iron mark of the Iron-Ring Cartel. Frost, ash, sealed wells, and the Cartel’s iron insignia recur in surviving depictions. These motifs are conventional representations and do not alter the recorded findings.
The Winter Reckoning carries an atmosphere of calculated treachery and poisoned victory. Its conclusion is therefore classified as a strategic success with concealed internal betrayal. The Iron-Ring Cartel remains the victor in the official reckoning; the poisoning of the wells of their own allies remains the concealed truth governing later interpretation.

Ancient noble dynasty claiming descent from the last Sunder-Kings.
House Morvain is an ancient noble house whose authority rests upon a
dynastic claim and the weight of its antiquity. It claims descent from
the last Sunder-Kings, a lineage asserted as the foundation of its
legitimacy. This claim is not presented as a secondary ornament to its
rule; it is the central doctrine by which the house defines its station
and expects recognition.

The house is seated at Ironfell Citadel. Its seat, identity, and
conduct conform to an aristocratic and kingly presentation shaped by
its claimed descent from the Sunder-Kings. Ceremonial display, heraldic
emphasis, and formal address are treated as instruments of continuity
rather than mere decoration. The house’s antiquity is itself a
political resource.
House Morvain carries itself with ancestral pride and a guarded sense
of entitlement. Its representatives are characterized by restraint,
formal reserve, and an expectation that precedence should be
acknowledged. Such conduct reflects the house’s view of itself as an
enduring dynasty rather than a temporary claimant among the powers of
the Ashen Era.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The record identifies House Morvain as belligerent in The War of
Endless Vigil. The record also identifies House Morvain as belligerent
in The Purge of Blackport. These entries establish the house’s
participation as a belligerent in both conflicts; they do not, in this
entry, define the full causes, operations, or outcomes of either.
House Morvain’s standing therefore derives from three mutually
reinforcing assertions: noble status, descent from the last
Sunder-Kings, and the accumulated authority of antiquity. Its posture
remains kingly in appearance, dynastic in doctrine, and guarded in
demeanor. The house’s claim is the basis upon which it presents its

Voltaire Hollowmere is a minor figure of the Ashen Era, born in 215 AS.
His recorded role is Falconer. He serves at Fenthrone and is a member
of The Ashen Vanguard.
The registry further records that Voltaire Hollowmere fought in The
Leaden Accord, fighting for The Ashen Vanguard. No additional account
of his duties during that conflict is preserved in this entry.
No canonical physical details are recorded for Voltaire Hollowmere. His
visual identity is associated with the work of a falconer: the
handling, tending, and deployment of trained birds are the principal
marks by which his station is represented in surviving records.
His canonical temperament is unrecorded. Statements concerning his
habits, loyalties beyond those explicitly listed, private conduct, or
personal history are therefore excluded from this registry.
Assessment: A service-bound figure of limited surviving documentation,
identified by his falconry, his station at Fenthrone, and his recorded
participation in The Leaden Accord under The Ashen Vanguard.

The Accord of Mournthrone
Classification: Conflict Beginning: 297 AS Ending: 301 AS Victor: The
Ashen Vanguard Recorded outcome: Collapsed into a decade of guerrilla
reprisals
The Accord of Mournthrone began in 297 AS and ended in 301 AS with The
Ashen Vanguard named victor. The title is retained in the annals
despite the accord’s failure to produce a durable settlement. Its
visual identity is that of a broken accord overshadowed by Mournthrone
and The Ashen Vanguard. Its demeanor is less that of a settled victory
than a sullen prelude to reprisal.
The principal recorded actions are as follows:

These entries do not describe a continuous advance or a conclusive
pacification. They establish the geographic record of the conflict and
the visible damage associated with its progress. The devastation of
Fenspire and Hollowvale remains attached to the conflict’s formal
chronology; the actions at Crookvale and Vharencrag Fortress remain
attached to its military record.
The declared result was victory for The Ashen Vanguard. The actual
result was less stable. The Accord of Mournthrone collapsed into a
decade of guerrilla reprisals, preserving the conflict in dispersed
violence after its formal ending. Accordingly, the designation of
victor does not constitute proof of complete control, reconciliation,
or lasting submission.
The concealed record gives the conflict a second interpretation. The
secret truth is that the losing commander was bribed to withdraw. This
fact alters the apparent meaning of the final result without removing
The Ashen Vanguard’s status as victor. The withdrawal is therefore
catalogued as a concealed cause of collapse rather than as a separate
engagement.
The numbered plate accompanying this entry preserves the recorded
figures. Consult the plate for those figures; they are not reproduced
here. For purposes of the annals, the essential determination remains
unchanged: The Accord of Mournthrone began in 297 AS, ended in 301 AS,
named The Ashen Vanguard victor, and left a decade of guerrilla

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Ashen Vanguard
The Ashen Vanguard is a knightly order sworn to contain the Ley-ruins
left by the Sundering. Its doctrine is not custodial in the passive
sense. It defines containment as an active military obligation,
requiring militant discipline, controlled force, and uninterrupted
vigilance wherever dangerous remnants persist.
Register Recorded designation
Faction The Ashen Vanguard
Org kind knightly order
Doctrine Militant order sworn to contain the
Ley-ruins left by the Sundering
Seat Vharenford
Disposition Severe, disciplined, constantly watchful
Recorded belligerencies The War of Drowned Light; The Accord of
Mournthrone; The Leaden Accord
Recorded outcome Victor of The Accord of Mournthrone
The Ashen Vanguard is seated at Vharenford. This seat is the principal
point from which its order is identified in surviving registers. No
distinction is made in those registers between its administrative
authority and its military purpose: both are subordinated to the
containment of the Ley-ruins.
Its visual identity is that of a militant, knightly order marked by the
grim legacy of the Ley-ruins. Equipment, bearing, and ceremony are
consequently treated as instruments of warning as much as instruments
of war. The order presents no softened interpretation of its charge.
Its appearance communicates the hazards it confronts and the severity
with which it addresses them.
The Vanguard’s demeanor is severe, disciplined, and constantly
watchful. Individual conduct is expected to reflect the order’s
collective doctrine. Uncertainty, negligence, and uncontrolled contact

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
with dangerous remnants are incompatible with its stated purpose. The
order therefore maintains a posture of readiness even when no
engagement is recorded.
The Ashen Vanguard was belligerent in The War of Drowned Light. It was
also belligerent in The Accord of Mournthrone, where The Ashen Vanguard
is recorded as victor. The order was further belligerent in The Leaden
Accord. These entries establish its recurring presence in the military
record without altering its primary classification as a knightly order.
In all formal descriptions, the central fact remains unchanged: The
Ashen Vanguard is a militant order sworn to contain the Ley-ruins left
by the Sundering. Its authority derives from that oath, its appearance

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Bleeding Crown
Identification
The Bleeding Crown is a royalist remnant fighting to restore the
shattered monarchy. Its cause is defined by loyalty to the monarchy and
opposition to the realm’s fractured condition. It does not recognize
the shattered condition of the realm as a legitimate settlement. Its
stated purpose is restoration rather than accommodation.
The Bleeding Crown is seated at Blackford. This seat constitutes its
established center of authority and the principal location from which
its royalist claim is maintained.
Doctrine and Temperament
Designation Record
Faction The Bleeding Crown
Org kind royalist remnant
Doctrine Royalist remnant fighting to restore the
shattered monarchy.
Seat Blackford
Demeanor Fervent, embittered, and determined
The faction’s loyalty is directed toward the monarchy as an
institution, not toward the realm’s present divisions. Its opposition
to the fractured condition of the realm informs its rhetoric,
recruitment, and conduct. In practice, the distinction between
restoration and reprisal is frequently narrow.
The Bleeding Crown is fervent in declaration and embittered by the
monarchy’s shattering. It is determined in pursuit of restoration.
These qualities are not ornamental descriptions; they are recognized
characteristics of the faction’s public bearing and internal
discipline.
Heraldic Aspect
Its visual identity is royalist and wounded, evoking a crown that has
endured the shattering of the monarchy. Crown forms, damaged regalia,
and marks of fracture are consistent with this presentation. The

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
symbolism presents survival as proof of rightful endurance. It does not
depict an unbroken crown. The wound is retained as evidence, warning,
and claim.
Recorded Belligerence
The Bleeding Crown was a belligerent in The War of Endless Vigil and is
recorded as its victor. The record establishes both its participation
and its victory; it does not diminish the faction’s character as a
remnant. Its success in that war is used by the faction as confirmation

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
table:

shattered monarchy.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
that the royalist cause remains capable of prevailing.
The Bleeding Crown was also a belligerent in The Accord of Mournthrone.
This designation records its presence as a party to that accord’s
belligerent order. No broader conclusion is entered here regarding the
accord’s settlement or subsequent force.
Assessment
The Bleeding Crown remains defined by restoration, monarchy, and
resistance to fragmentation. Its authority is royalist in origin,
wounded in appearance, and fervent, embittered, and determined in
demeanor. Codex classification: royalist remnant.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Iron-Ring Cartel
The Iron-Ring Cartel is a merchant cartel seated at Hollowreach. Its
doctrine is recorded as follows:
> The Iron-Ring Cartel — doctrine: Mercantile league running contraband
through the ruined trade roads.
The Cartel is a mercantile league organized around commerce conducted
across the remnants of the realm’s trade routes. Its operations concern
the movement, exchange, and concealment of contraband through roads
damaged or abandoned after the Sundering. The organization’s structure
is consequently commercial rather than feudal, with authority expressed
through control of trade, access, and passage.
Its visual identity is mercantile and hard-edged. Iron, sealed cargo,
marked ledgers, guarded wagons, and reinforced trade gear are
consistent with its cartel structure and contraband trade. These signs
are not ornamental. They indicate a faction whose public identity is
inseparable from the practical demands of commerce conducted beyond
lawful channels.
The Cartel’s demeanor is calculating and practical. It is comfortable
operating beyond lawful trade and does not present illegality as a
moral distinction requiring explanation. Decisions are assessed by
utility, risk, access, and return. Negotiation is therefore treated as
an instrument of commerce rather than a display of trust.

primary classification. The Iron-Ring Cartel remains a merchant cartel,
and its stated doctrine remains the operation of a mercantile league
running contraband through the ruined trade roads.
At Hollowreach, its seated authority is understood through this same
commercial logic. The Cartel’s presence is defined by transaction,
movement, and controlled access. Its hard-edged appearance and
calculating demeanor are functional expressions of its organization,

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Leaden Accord
Classification: Conflict Beginning: 330 AS End: 342 AS Recorded
casualty figure: 14011 Named victor: The Iron-Ring Cartel
The Leaden Accord was a prolonged military contest whose surviving
record is defined less by conquest than by erasure. Its duration began
in 330 AS and ended in 342 AS. The accepted outcome names The Iron-Ring
Cartel as victor. This designation remains official despite the final
destruction suffered by both opposing hosts.
Recorded site Year Assessment
Greyfell Citadel 337 AS Devastated by The Leaden
Accord
Palewell Abbey 338 AS Devastated by The Leaden
Accord
Cindermere Hold 338 AS Devastated by The Leaden
Accord
Vharencrag Fortress 341 AS The Leaden Accord waged
there
The Leaden Accord ended when both hosts were destroyed by a Ley-storm.
The event rendered the declaration of victory administratively useful
but militarily hollow. The recorded casualty figure is 14011. No
surviving account establishes the final disposition of every combatant,
and the visible remains support only the conclusion that mutual ruin
followed the last engagement.
The principal contradiction lies in the artifact associated with the
conflict. Public accounts state that it was destroyed. The hidden truth
is that a supposedly destroyed artifact was in fact spirited away. Its
absence is therefore treated as evidence of concealment rather than
confirmation of destruction. The identity and present custody of the
artifact are not established in this entry.
The Leaden Accord’s visual identity is leaden, storm-riven, and haunted

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
by the absence of a supposedly destroyed artifact. Surviving depictions
favor dim metal, fractured skies, vacant reliquaries, and structures
reduced to inert silhouettes. These conventions do not signify a single
battlefield; they signify the conflict’s condition of incomplete
closure.
Its demeanor is the bleak stillness of mutual ruin concealed beneath a
declared victory. This distinction is preserved in formal annotations:
victory belongs to The Iron-Ring Cartel, while the hosts themselves
were destroyed by a Ley-storm. The declaration and the destruction are
both canonical, but they do not describe the same kind of success.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The devastation of Greyfell Citadel in 337 AS, Palewell Abbey in 338
AS, and Cindermere Hold in 338 AS marks the conflict’s destructive
record. The engagement at Vharencrag Fortress in 341 AS stands as its
last specifically recorded site before the ending in 342 AS.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Purge of Blackport
Classification: Conflict Period: 311 AS–321 AS Victor: The Iron-Ring
Cartel Casualties: 70907 Outcome: Ended with the total rout of the
aggressors
The Purge of Blackport began in 311 AS and ended in 321 AS. It caused
70907 casualties and ended with the total rout of the aggressors. The
Iron-Ring Cartel emerged as victor.
The conflict’s recorded scope includes two designated theatres of
devastation:
Record Entry
Blackport Subject to the purge
Fenspire The Purge of Blackport waged at Fenspire
(in 319 AS)
Gloamreach The Purge of Blackport devastated
Gloamreach (in 320 AS)
The official settlement attributes victory to The Iron-Ring Cartel and
treats the rout of the aggressors as the conclusive military result.
The record is therefore commonly cited as a model of merciless triumph:
decisive, comprehensive, and without mitigation.
A concealed truth alters that judgment. The victors poisoned the wells
of their own allies. This act is not presented as a secondary accident
or an incidental contamination. It is the hidden instrument by which
the apparent triumph must be understood. The same force that secured
victory imposed ruin upon those aligned with it.
The Purge of Blackport has consequently retained two simultaneous
classifications in the annals. Publicly, it is a victorious campaign
ending in the total rout of the aggressors. In restricted accounts, it
is a calculated betrayal concealed beneath the language of victory. The
distinction is material: the casualty figure records the scale of the

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
conflict, but does not by itself disclose the method used by the
victors.
Appearance: Blackport under purge, marked by The Iron-Ring Cartel and
poisoned water.
Demeanor: Merciless triumph soured by calculated betrayal.
The conflict’s enduring emblem is thus not the routed aggressor, nor
the Cartel’s undisputed victory alone, but poisoned water within a
victorious domain. Its records remain serviceable for determining
dates, theatres, casualties, and outcome. They are less reliable when
used to describe the moral character of the victory.

chunks.text:
The Silent Choir
Classification Record
Faction The Silent Choir
The Silent Choir - org kind priesthood
The Silent Choir - doctrine Secretive priesthood that records,
censors, and rewrites history.
Seat The Silent Choir seated at Vharencrag
Fortress

Drowned Light; The Silent Choir victor of
The War of Drowned Light

The Winter Reckoning The Silent Choir belligerent in The Winter

Office and Authority
The Silent Choir is a secretive priesthood whose religious authority is
exercised through control of the historical record. Its doctrine
assigns record, correction, suppression, and revision to a single
sacred function. History is therefore not treated as a fixed
inheritance. It is maintained as an instrument of order, subject to
examination and alteration by the Choir.
The Silent Choir records history. It censors history. It rewrites
history. These duties are not separate offices in the known account of
the faction, but expressions of one doctrine. The Choir’s authority
rests upon possession of the accepted version of events and upon the
restriction of competing versions.
The Silent Choir is seated at Vharencrag Fortress. Its seat is
associated with restrained religious practice, controlled access, and
the keeping of records. The visual identity of The Silent Choir is
priestly, restrained, and defined by secrecy and the keeping of
records. Its appearance communicates neither pageantry nor open force.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
It presents the discipline of custody.
Conduct
The Choir is quiet, inscrutable, and deliberate in its handling of
truth. Statements are measured. Omissions are consequential. Disclosure
is treated as an act requiring the same care as inscription. The
faction’s silence is therefore not an absence of policy; it is a method
of policy.
Its custodians maintain a severe distinction between what may be
preserved, what may be concealed, and what may be rewritten. The

censors, and rewrites history.

Fortress

chunks.text:
distinction is administered through religious authority rather than
public consent. For this reason, the Choir’s records possess both
archival and doctrinal weight.
War Register
The Silent Choir was belligerent in The War of Drowned Light and was
victor of The War of Drowned Light. The Silent Choir was belligerent in
The War of Endless Vigil. The Silent Choir was belligerent in The
Winter Reckoning.
No general account of these belligerencies is entered here beyond the
stated record. The Choir’s own handling of the historical record
remains a material consideration in all surviving accounts. Its victory
in The War of Drowned Light is therefore recorded as an established
factional result, while the form and interpretation of that result
remain subject to the Choir’s doctrine.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The War of Drowned Light
Classification: Conflict Period: 225 AS–235 AS Casualties: 64617
Recorded victor: The Silent Choir Outcome: Collapsed into a decade of
guerrilla reprisals
The War of Drowned Light began in 225 AS and ended in 235 AS. Its
duration is recorded without qualification, though the violence
associated with it did not resolve into a clean termination. The War of
Drowned Light collapsed into a decade of guerrilla reprisals, and its
conclusion therefore signifies the end of the principal war rather than
the restoration of settled order.
The conflict’s recorded casualty figure is 64617. This figure is
preserved in the annals as the accepted total for the war. The
surviving record does not treat the number as evidence of a decisive
engagement or a single catastrophic event. Instead, it belongs to a
campaign remembered for attrition, concealed operations, reprisals, and
the persistence of violence after formal hostilities had ended.
Year Recorded occurrence

Gloamreach.

Cindermere Hold.

Citadel.

The War of Drowned Light victor was The Silent Choir. This designation
remains the formal outcome in the principal annalistic tradition. A
separate concealed record states that the spark that started it was
staged by The Silent Choir. The victory and the secret staging are
therefore entered together, though the latter was not presented as

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
public cause during the conflict.
Its visual identity is one of drowned radiance, broken banners, and a
war remembered through reprisals rather than triumph. Records
concerning its battlefields frequently emphasize obscured light,
damaged standards, and the absence of ceremonial closure. These
features are classificatory rather than decorative: they distinguish
the conflict from wars whose memory is organized around conquest or
formal settlement.
Its demeanor is marked by concealed treachery, attrition, and
unresolved vengeance. The designation applies both to the war itself
and to its aftermath. The decade of guerrilla reprisals remains the
principal reason the conflict is not treated as concluded in the

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The War of Endless Vigil
Classification: Conflict Period: 247 AS–251 AS Recorded victor: The
Bleeding Crown Casualty figure: 81577
The War of Endless Vigil began in 247 AS and ended in 251 AS. Its
recorded conclusion was the total rout of the aggressors. The Bleeding
Crown is recorded as the victor.
The conflict imposed severe destruction across the contested
territories. The War of Endless Vigil devastated Crookvale in 249 AS.
It devastated Thorncairn in 250 AS. The War of Endless Vigil was waged
at Hollowreach in 251 AS.
Register Record
Conflict The War of Endless Vigil
Beginning 247 AS
Ending 251 AS
Casualties 81577
Outcome Ended with the total rout of the
aggressors
Victor The Bleeding Crown
Secret truth The losing commander was bribed to
withdraw
Recorded sites Crookvale; Hollowreach; Thorncairn
Operational Character
The war’s visual identity is one of blood-marked watchfulness,
exhausted armies, and an enemy line breaking under prolonged vigilance.
Its imagery is therefore defined less by sudden triumph than by the
persistence of forces that remain at their stations until opposition
fails.
The conflict feels brutal and decisive on the surface. Its recorded
outcome supports that appearance: the aggressors were totally routed,
and The Bleeding Crown received the formal victory. This conclusion is
not, however, a complete account of the war’s conduct.
Concealed Determinant
The secret truth of the War of Endless Vigil is that the losing
commander was bribed to withdraw. The withdrawal remains the concealed

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
determinant behind the apparent final collapse. Accordingly, the war is
classified as both a decisive rout and a corrupted victory.
This distinction is preserved in the annals without altering the
official result. The Bleeding Crown remains the recorded victor. The
total rout of the aggressors remains the recorded outcome. The hidden

chunks.text:
payment does not nullify either entry; it qualifies the means by which
the conclusion was reached.
The casualty figure is recorded as 81577. The devastation of Crookvale,
the devastation of Thorncairn, and the fighting at Hollowreach
establish the war’s material imprint across its listed sites. Together
with the concealed bribery, these records define the conflict as an
episode of prolonged vigilance, exhaustion, betrayal, and final
collapse.

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
The Winter Reckoning
Classification: Conflict Period: 270 AS–283 AS Victor: The Iron-Ring
Cartel Casualty figure: 27987
The Winter Reckoning began in 270 AS and ended in 283 AS. Its duration
is recorded without interruption in the surviving annals, though the
record of its final settlement remains materially incomplete. The
conflict left 27987 casualties and concluded with The Iron-Ring Cartel
identified as victor.
Its outcome was decided by a betrayal at the eleventh hour. This
determination is accepted by the principal accounts, despite their
disagreement concerning the identity and scope of the treachery. The
concealed truth is that the victors poisoned the wells of their own
allies. This fact is preserved in restricted testimony and is not
treated as a battlefield rumor.
Recorded site Year Register

at Stormmarch (in 276 AS)
Gloammarch 277 AS The Winter Reckoning waged
at Gloammarch (in 277 AS)

(in 271 AS)

(in 277 AS)
The documented sites indicate a conflict marked by movement through
exposed winter ground, fortified holdings, and contested sources of
water. No single surviving account establishes the full sequence of
engagements. The destruction of Cindermere Hold and Marrowwell Abbey is
nevertheless entered as a direct consequence of the conflict’s passage.
Its visual identity is one of winter, betrayal, and the iron mark of

chunks.doc_title: The Annals of the Ashen Era
chunks.text:
the Iron-Ring Cartel. Frost, ash, sealed wells, and the Cartel’s iron
insignia recur in surviving depictions. These motifs are conventional
representations and do not alter the recorded findings.
The Winter Reckoning carries an atmosphere of calculated treachery and
poisoned victory. Its conclusion is therefore classified as a strategic
success with concealed internal betrayal. The Iron-Ring Cartel remains
the victor in the official reckoning; the poisoning of the wells of
their own allies remains the concealed truth governing later
interpretation.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Ashreach Sale
chunks.text:
Catalogue of the Ashreach Sale
A Marsh-Holding Offered Under Seal, with Conditions of Contest
> To all creditors, claimants, captains, and persons of sound enough judgment to bid: > Let it be
known that Ashreach is presented for auction—not as a jewel, nor as a refuge, but as a defended holding in
a country where water remembers every footprint. > —From the hand of the appointed catalogue-keeper
The Holding Entire
Ashreach lies in The Weeping Marshes and is currently contested. Its garrison numbers 2598, making
it a defended but unsettled holding rather than a core stronghold.
The prudent bidder will read those words twice.
The walls—where wall may be distinguished from bank, bank from ruin, and ruin from drowned
foundation—are offered with the settlement. So too the perpetual burden of watchfulness. Ashreach
presents the bleak, marsh-bound aspect of a settlement caught between ash and water. Its atmosphere is
tense, unstable, and perpetually threatened.
No claim is made here that the holding is peaceful. No claim is made that it is safe. The catalogue merely
records that it stands, and that standing in The Weeping Marshes is itself a form of defiance.
Lot A — The Ashen Ground
An extent of blackened earth and wet margin, suitable to those who prefer their inheritance difficult to
reach and more difficult to keep. Mist is included without surcharge. The mud is deep, the air close, and
the horizon frequently unwilling to appear.
The lot is offered as part of Ashreach and may not be separated from its unsettled condition.
Lot B — The Garrison
The garrison numbers 2598.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Ashreach Sale
chunks.text:
Arms, discipline, loyalties, and appetites are not warranted by this catalogue. The catalogue-keeper
records only the number and leaves the buyer to discover what manner of defense is purchased with it.
A defended holding is not thereby a secure holding. Any clerk who says otherwise has never slept beneath
a roof while the marsh whispered against the door.
Lot C — The Claim
Ashreach is offered amid the broader contention over the ruins by The Ashen Vanguard, House
Morvain, the Silent Choir, the Iron-Ring Cartel, and the Bleeding Crown.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Ashreach Sale
chunks.text:
Their interest, if interest it be, is not represented as consent, surrender, or absence. The holding remains
currently contested, and bidders are advised that ink has less weight than steel when both are set upon the
same boundary.
Final Notice
Ashreach is not sold as a core stronghold. It is sold as a defended but unsettled holding: bleak,
marsh-bound, caught between ash and water, tense, unstable, and perpetually threatened.
Bids shall be spoken plainly.
The marsh has little patience for mumbling.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of Lantern and Ledger — Draven Ashgrove
chunks.text:
Catalogue of Lantern and Ledger — Draven Ashgrove
& Halvard Sablewood
Issued beneath the soot-black seal of the auction hall, for those who prize a name more highly than a face.
Draven Ashgrove

Lantern-Warden.

Lantern-Warden. Thus the imagination supplies what the record withholds: the lamp before the face, the

assumptions under Draven Ashgrove’s name.

Halvard Sablewood
Description: A minor figure of the Ashen Era, born in 408 AS. Halvard Sablewood serves as a scribe.
Nature of the Offering: Offered here is the scribe’s standing as a keeper of written matter: the authority

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of Lantern and Ledger — Draven Ashgrove
chunks.text:
suggested by a hand that copies, marks, preserves, and perhaps outlasts the mouths of the living. No
manuscript, quill, desk, robe, or private document is included. The catalogue sells the account, not the

Appearance: No canonical physical details are recorded. His visual identity is associated with the

Condition: Unadorned, incomplete, and resistant to embellishment. The record bears what it bears. The

chunks.doc_title: **The Greyfell Catalogue of Abandoned Stone**
chunks.text:
### *An Auction of Salvage, Relics, and Unclaimed Remnants from Greyfell Citadel*
> **To all creditors, collectors, oath-breakers, and persons of sufficient nerve:**  
> The following catalogue concerns the remains of Greyfell Citadel, founded in **62 AS** within the **Shattered Vale**. The Citadel is abandoned and lies outside the realm’s core holdings. No warranty is offered regarding sanctity, safety, ownership, or the continued good sense of any purchaser.
Greyfell is not presented as a handsome ruin. Its visual identity is one of grey stone and grey-hued collapse, rising from the Shattered Vale like a tooth left in a dead jaw. Whatever banners once hung there have been taken by weather or hand. Whatever garrison once watched the approaches has gone. The place retains the demeanor of an old desolation, its former stronghold status reduced to abandonment.
The auctioneer records that each offering has been removed from the Citadel or its immediate fallen works. Buyers shall judge the truth of this claim according to their own consciences.
---
## **Catalogue of Offerings**
### **The Gatehouse Ironwork**
Bent hinges, corroded fastenings, and a length of darkened bar. Useful to those who desire the appearance of old authority without the burden of maintaining a gate.
### **The Grey Chapel Stone**
A dressed block bearing shallow marks too worn for confident reading. It has been cleaned only of loose dirt. The purchaser is advised not to ask what prayers were once spoken over it.

chunks.doc_title: **The Greyfell Catalogue of Abandoned Stone**
chunks.text:
### **The Watch-Seat**
A broken stone chair from an upper passage, with one arm intact. It is uncomfortable, cold, and entirely suited to the ruling temperament.
### **The Ashen Archive Board**
A warped board with traces of pegs and cord. No papers accompany it. Its former purpose is unknown, which makes it desirable to those who prefer mystery to evidence.
### **The Cistern Chain**
A length of iron chain, heavily scaled, offered as found. Whether it served water, prisoners, or some uglier need cannot be established.
### **The Valeward Shards**
Fragments of grey masonry gathered from a collapsed outer wall. They are suitable for memorials, thresholds, grave-markers, or the construction of another place destined to be abandoned.
### **The Unclaimed Standard-Rod**
A splintered staff with no surviving device. The wood is darkened, the metal collar pitted. It bears no readable allegiance.
### **The Citadel Dust**
Sealed in a plain vessel. The catalogue clerk insists it is masonry dust. The clerk has not opened the vessel.
---
All sales are final. No purchaser may claim that Greyfell Citadel was misrepresented: it is a ruin of grey stone in the Shattered Vale, founded in **62 AS**, abandoned, and outside the realm’s core holdings. Its silence is included without additional charge.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Ashen Gavel: Papers, Signals, and a Vale Under Watch
chunks.section: Catalogue of the Ashen Gavel: Papers, Signals, and a Vale Under Watch
chunks.text: Issued for the consideration of bidders who prize dangerous knowledge above comfort. Provenance is sworn only where plainly stated; all other descriptions remain the house’s judgment.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Ashen Gavel: Papers, Signals, and a Vale Under Watch
chunks.text:
A modest parcel of copied leaves, ruled scraps, and sealed blanks, offered as an evocation of Halvard Sablewood, a minor figure of the Ashen Era. The leaves bear no boast of authorship. Their value lies in the habits they suggest: ordered margins, patient corrections, and the cold discipline of a hand trained to preserve what stronger folk would burn.
Halvard Sablewood was born in 408 AS. He serves as a scribe. No canonical physical details are recorded for him; his visual identity is associated with the work of a scribe. His canonical temperament is unrecorded.
The house warns bidders against purchasing a face where none has been given, or a personality where the record is silent. What is offered is the shadow of a vocation: ink, sequence, silence, and the keeping of other people’s words.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Ashen Gavel: Papers, Signals, and a Vale Under Watch
chunks.text:
A sealed packet of naval-form memoranda, offered under the name and station of Morwenna Ashgrove. The contents are not opened before bidding. Such restraint is prudent when the subject is a major Fleet Admiral whose authority is disciplined on the surface and darkened beneath it.
Morwenna Ashgrove was born in 288 AS. She is a major Fleet Admiral. Morwenna secretly sells intelligence to the Iron-Ring Cartel.
No canonical physical features are established. Her visual identity is defined by the commanding station of Fleet Admiral. Her demeanor projects disciplined authority shadowed by covert dealings.
The packet is therefore sold not as a portrait, but as a danger: command rendered into paper, loyalty folded into trade, and silence made profitable. Bidders are advised that secrecy is not the same as safety.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Ashen Gavel: Papers, Signals, and a Vale Under Watch
chunks.text:
A charcoal prospectus of Hollowvale, its walls and approaches rendered beneath the black sweep of the Blood-Moor. The drawing presents a defended vale surrounded by ominous country, with watchfulness built into every ridge and gate.
Hollowvale was founded in 286 AS in the Blood-Moor. It is garrisoned by 7,594 troops and remains outside the realm’s core holdings.
Its visual identity is that of a defended vale encircled by the Blood-Moor’s threatening landscape. Its demeanor is guarded vigilance, sustained by a substantial garrison.
The prospectus contains no promise of welcome. It offers instead the hard comfort of walls, sentries, and distance from the realm’s core holdings. Those who bid should remember: a place may stand apart without standing free.
The auction house accepts no blame for knowledge acquired, secrets exposed, or valleys that continue to watch after the lamps are extinguished.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Unadorned Record: Isolde Mournvale
chunks.text:
Offered under the Ashen Era’s customary rule that a name may be weighed even when no treasure attends it, this entry concerns Isolde Mournvale, a minor figure of the Ashen Era.
She was born in 341 AS.
The surviving record gives her service plainly: Isolde Mournvale serves as a falconer. Beyond this office, the catalogue must proceed with an empty hand. No authenticated portrait, signet, garment, weapon, feather, hood, glove, or other possession is attached to her entry here. Buyers who seek painted eyes, noble blood, battlefield distinction, or a tale sharpened by repetition are warned that none may be supplied from the record.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Unadorned Record: Isolde Mournvale
chunks.text:
No canonical physical details are recorded for Isolde Mournvale.
Her visual identity is therefore not fixed by face, height, scars, coloring, age, or dress. It is associated instead with the work of a falconer: the discipline of handling a hunting bird, the patience required before release, and the silent attention given to a creature that may depart without farewell. These are the signs by which artists, chroniclers, and household rememberers may imagine her office, but they must not be mistaken for recorded features of her person.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Unadorned Record: Isolde Mournvale
chunks.text:
Isolde Mournvale’s canonical temperament is unrecorded.
The catalogue offers no judgment concerning her courage, cruelty, loyalty, wit, piety, obedience, or temper. Any seller who praises her gentleness, condemns her severity, or claims that she loved or feared anything speaks beyond the warrant of this entry. Such claims may be recited in taverns, painted upon banners, or whispered beside a mews, but they do not belong to the authenticated description.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Unadorned Record: Isolde Mournvale
chunks.text:
The name is legible. The birth year is given. The occupation is given. The remainder is silence.
This silence is not damage to be repaired by ornament. It is the present condition of the record concerning Isolde Mournvale. No estimate is placed upon her renown, for the catalogue establishes none. No provenance is claimed beyond the statement that she is a minor figure of the Ashen Era. No likeness is guaranteed, and no demeanor may be inferred as fact.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Unadorned Record: Isolde Mournvale
chunks.text: The successful claimant receives neither a body nor a legend, but an entry bounded by what can be said. Let the buyer remember: where the record ends, invention begins.

Catalogue of Ashen Relics and Persons of Note
For the Consideration of Bidders Beneath a Sound Roof
Entry: Lucan Hollowmere
Name: Lucan Hollowmere Calling: Herbalist Birth: 296 AS
Lucan Hollowmere is entered here as a minor figure of the Ashen Era, though the hand that prepared this
catalogue admits that “minor” is a judgment made by the living and not always trusted by the dead.
He serves as an Herbalist. Beyond that service, the records grow thin. No canonical physical details are
recorded for Lucan Hollowmere. His visual identity is associated with the work of an herbalist: gathered
leaves, bitter roots, stained vessels, and the patient sorting of what heals from what merely delays the
grave.
His demeanor is unrecorded. Buyers are therefore cautioned against purchasing imagined gentleness,
secret cruelty, or any other temperament attributed to him by tavern mouths and idle ink.
This entry concerns the recorded figure, not a likeness, relic, or sworn testimony. Any claimant who
insists that Lucan Hollowmere’s hands, eyes, voice, or manner are known speaks beyond the catalogue.
Entry: Ederon Fellgard
Name: Ederon Fellgard Calling: Sapper Birth: 338 AS
Ederon Fellgard is likewise a minor figure of the Ashen Era. He serves as a Sapper, a calling whose tools
are more readily recognized than the person who carries them.
No canonical physical traits or distinctive visual features are established for Ederon Fellgard. No
canonical temperament or emotional disposition is established for Ederon Fellgard either. The catalogue

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of Ashen Relics and Persons of Note
chunks.text:
will not supply what the record withholds. Buyers may inspect the absence of description and value it
according to conscience, superstition, or purse.
No personal association between Ederon Fellgard and Lucan Hollowmere is certified in these pages.
Entry: The Sceptre of Final Winter
Designation: The Sceptre of Final Winter Class: Ward Forged: 87 AS Attunement cost: 55
The Sceptre of Final Winter is a ward forged in 87 AS. Its visual identity is that of a ward bearing the
name The Sceptre of Final Winter; no further canonical form is established here. Let no eager bidder
mistake ornament for evidence.
Attunement to it costs 55.
It radiates an atmosphere of cold finality. Whether this is warning, promise, or merely the faithful nature
of the ward cannot be settled by the catalogue keeper. Those who approach are advised to bring steady
hands and no expectation of warmth.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Unseen Sapper: Morwenna Vosgard
chunks.text:
**Being a modest offering of records, impressions, and empty places concerning Morwenna Vosgard, minor character of the Ashen Era**
Let the buyer be warned: this catalogue contains no portrait. No physical features are recorded for **Morwenna Vosgard**. Her visual identity is associated with the work of a **Sapper**, and no faithful likeness may therefore be promised beneath any hood, mask, or veil.
The five powers of the realm remain named upon the margins of this sale: **the Ashen Vanguard, House Morvain, the Silent Choir, the Iron-Ring Cartel, and the Bleeding Crown**. Whether any would claim this material is not recorded. Whether any would deny it is likewise not recorded.
---
### Lot A — Birth Entry, 296 AS
A plain leaf bearing the single useful certainty of this catalogue:
> **Morwenna Vosgard was born in 296 AS.**
The hand is cramped, the ink faded, and the surrounding entries offer no clarification. This is not offered as proof of lineage, station, or allegiance. It establishes only the year given above.
---
### Lot B — The Sapper’s Mark
A collection of indistinct impressions: scored earth, broken stone, a darkened tool-head, and the suggestion of labor performed where labor is least praised.
These images are not portraits. They are offered because Morwenna Vosgard’s visual identity is associated with the work of a Sapper. The catalogue makes no claim that these objects were hers, that she touched them, or that they were present at any particular undertaking.
The discerning bidder will observe that absence may be the most honest likeness available.

chunks.doc_title: Catalogue of the Unseen Sapper: Morwenna Vosgard
chunks.text:
### Lot C — Service Description
A narrow strip of vellum, undated and without seal, reading:
> **Morwenna Vosgard serves as a Sapper.**
No rank is supplied. No employer is supplied. No account of her duties is supplied beyond the title of her service. Buyers are urged to resist the common hunger to make a life from a single occupation.
---
### Lot D — Temperament, Unentered
A blank folio, carefully preserved.
No temperament is recorded for Morwenna Vosgard. The folio contains neither praise nor accusation, neither tenderness nor spite. It is not evidence of gentleness, cruelty, courage, fear, obedience, or defiance. It is simply the place where such testimony fails to appear.
---
### Lot E — The Absent Portrait
An empty frame, offered without image.
This final lot gathers the catalogue’s several deficiencies: no physical features recorded, no temperament recorded, and no further particulars that may safely be declared. It is presented for those who understand that a minor character may still cast a long shadow—though this catalogue cannot say where that shadow falls.
**Bidding shall proceed in silence.**

Accordingly, no portrait, likeness, or character assessment is offered under his name. Any seller claiming to know the cast of his face, the color of his eyes, the weight of his hand, or the temper of his soul is selling smoke.

chunks.doc_title: Ballad Concerning Crookgate Keep
chunks.text:
THE CROOKED STONE AND THE THORNWALD STANDARD
O hush, hush now, the marsh-wind sighs, Where drowned reeds bow
beneath grey skies; Let no man swear what waits beyond The broken
palisade and pond.
For Crookgate Keep stands grim and lean, Against the Weeping
Marshes’ mien; Its stones wear rain, its towers stare Through
vapour, mud, and rotting air.
Founded in 294 AS, It keeps no peace, grants no redress; Contested
still, it holds its ground Where uncertain waters crawl around.
It lies outside the realm’s core holdings, Beyond the bells and
guarded mouldings; No lord may claim its stones by right, Nor name
its shadow day or night,
Some say the walls remember feet, Some say the gate has learned
deceit; I say the keep has neither tongue— Yet every door is
listening.
O hush, hush now, the marsh-wind grieves, It combs the rushes,
shakes the eaves; At Crookgate, truth is thin as thread, And every
path may end among the dead.
But hear another burden rise, Beneath the iron-coloured skies: A
standard lifted, straight and high, A solemn mark that will not fly
Isolde Thornwald bears it still— So sings the road, so wills the
hill; Isolde Thornwald, Standard-Bearer, With formal step and
shoulders fairer.
Born in 272 AS, She learned no bow to ease distress; Her face is
set, her bearing plain, Her hands hold fast through wind and rain
Not for the feast, nor lordly hall, Not for the trumpet’s idle call;
She stands where watching eyes are turned, While lesser courage
folds and burns.
The cloth may snap, the dark may roar, The mud may clutch the

chunks.doc_title: Ballad Concerning Crookgate Keep
chunks.text:
standard’s floor; Still does she raise that sign above The nameless
fear, the faithless love.
O Crookgate stone, O thorn-marked sign, Your fates are joined in

chunks.doc_title: Ballad Concerning Crookgate Keep
chunks.text:
song, not mine; I bind you here with cord of rhyme, Though no man

bind the marsh or time.

The keep stands watch in uncertain weather, The standard bears its

burden better; One is a fortress, stark and old, One is a vow that

will not fold.

&

If Crookgate falls, let no bell toll— The marsh keeps count within

its soul. If Isolde’s standard dims at last, Sing not that

steadfastness has passed.

For stones may sink in soaking ground, And banners tear without a

sound; Yet while one throat remembers clear, The keep and standard

both are near.

So hush, hush now, you reed and rain, Carry this song through mist

and pain: Crookgate Keep, where doubts abide— Isolde Thornwald,

standing wide.

chunks.doc_title: Ballad Concerning The Sceptre Of Final Winter
chunks.text:
THE BALLAD OF THE SCEPTRE OF FINAL WINTER
Come close, my ash-clad brothers, Come near, you frost-bitten few;
The fire is low, the road is lost, And the night is looking through.
I sing of a ward in a shuttered hall, Where the dead leaves claw the
stone— The Sceptre of Final Winter, And the silence it calls its
own.
No crown was set upon its brow, No oath was carved in gold; Yet men
grew still beside its shape, And women’s blood ran cold. Its visual
identity is that of a ward Bearing the name that all tongues fear: @
The Sceptre of Final Winter, Though no warm name may linger near.
It was forged in 87 AS, So the old black tablets say. I have not
seen the hands that wrought it; I have not lived that day. But the
iron remembers, or so we swear, And the stone remembers too— The
Sceptre of Final Winter, With a hush in all it knew.
“Who shall dare to take it up?” The starving sentry cried. “Who
shal] pay the hidden price And stand with frost inside?” The answer
passed from mouth to mouth, A tithe no priest could mend: Attunement
to it costs 55, And none can name the end.
Some call it mercy, some call it doom, Some call it merely a ward. I
call it the last shut door At the edge of the world. For it radiates
an atmosphere Of cold finality; Not rage, nor grief, nor triumph—
Only what must cease tu be.
I saw it once—perhaps I dreamed; The moon was a broken bowl. Its
shadow lay across the floor Like winter over a soul. No blade was
drawn, no bell was struck, No herald gave command; Still every
breath became a prayer, And dust forgot the hand.

chunks.doc_title: Ballad Concerning The Sceptre Of Final Winter
chunks.text:
O Sceptre of Final Winter, Ward of the closing sky, Keep your
counsel in the frozen dark, Let the fevered kingdoms die. If you are
doom, then doom is clean; If mercy, mercy’s thin. The cold is
waiting past the door, And the cold will let none in.
So sing no praise at the Sceptre’s name, Nor curse it in the rain. A
ward may bear what hearts cannot, And silence outlast pain. Remember
87 AS, remember 55, Remember the final hue— The Sceptre of Final
Winter, And the winter waiting through.

chunks.doc_title: Contract Concerning Halvard Sablewood
chunks.text:
COVENANT OF INK AND DUE RECORD CONCERNING HALVARD SABLEWOOL
Let this instrument be read before witnesses, seal-bearers, and al]
who have cause to trust the written word.
@
The person called Halvard Sablewood, a minor figure of the Ashen
Era, is hereby received into the keeping of the undersigned house,
office, or claimant, whose name may be entered beside the seal when
this covenant is witnessed. This covenant concerns the faithful
exercise of his craft and shall be judged by the marks he makes, not
by rumor, appearance, or temper.
It is entered into the record that Halvard Sablewood was born in 408
AS. It is further entered that he serves aa scribe. His hand,
therefore, shall be lent to the setting down of testimony,
inventories, oaths, accounts, petitions, condemnations, pardons, and
such other matter as is placed before him under lawful instruction.
He shall preserve the meaning of every dictated word. Where a
passage is broken, doubtful, sealed, or beyond his authority to
amend, he shall mark the defect rather than conceal it. He shall not
alter a name, measure, debt, boundary, confession, or judgment for
favor, fear, hunger, payment, or threat. If commanded to make a
copy, he shall distinguish copy from original. If commanded to
destroy a record, he'shall seek the command in writing before
applying blade, flame, water, or ash.
All leaves, scraps, tablets, bindings, seals, pigments, and
instruments entrusted to his care shall remain the property of the
party that entrusted them, unless another disposition is written

chunks.doc_title: Contract Concerning Halvard Sablewood
chunks.text:
upon this covenant. A record completed by his hand shall not be
removed, hidden, exchanged, or shown to an unpermitted reader
without leave from the authority that commissioned it.
No description of Halvard Sablewood’s physical appearance is
